playbook.escalate: Suggested: a new country, or any fallback on consent, goes to the Head of Legal with the CRO and the CISO, and to the outsourcing committee where the Services are material, with a decision on whether to consult the HKMA first (SA-2 1.3.2).

terms.title: Governing law
terms.summary: For overseas outsourcing, SA-2 prefers the agreement to be governed by Hong Kong law. It is a preference, not an absolute rule.
require: **Hong Kong law:** preferably Hong Kong law for an overseas outsourcing agreement (SA-2 2.9.1).
drafting: **If foreign law is unavoidable:** record why, and widen the scope of the local-law opinion (SA-2 2.9.1 asks for one only on overseas authorities' access to customer data) to confirm that the HKMA access, audit and termination clauses are enforceable under that law. Even under Hong Kong law, the opinion should cover any blocking or secrecy law where the vendor or its group is incorporated or the data sits, since choosing Hong Kong law does not displace them. This is counsel's drafting, not an SA-2 requirement.

playbook.why: SA-2 2.9.1, a non-statutory guidance note, says an overseas outsourcing agreement should preferably be governed by Hong Kong law. It is a preference, so foreign law can be accepted with a documented rationale and, for material outsourcing, a local-law opinion. Forum and process agent are counsel's drafting; the Regulator carve-out applies SA-2 2.8.2 and Digital Bank Guideline para 23.
preferred: **Hong Kong law:** Hong Kong law governs the agreement, every document it incorporates and any non-contractual claims connected with them (SA-2 2.9.1).

**Hong Kong forum:** Hong Kong courts, or arbitration seated in Hong Kong where the Supplier's assets sit in a country that may not enforce Hong Kong judgments (counsel's drafting). Check enforceability as part of the local-law opinion.
**Process agent:** an offshore Supplier appoints an agent in Hong Kong to accept service of proceedings, and replaces it promptly if the appointment ends (counsel's drafting).

**Regulator carve-out:** no dispute step, forum or confidentiality of proceedings stops either party disclosing to or cooperating with a Regulator (applying SA-2 2.8.2). The Supplier keeps performing, and does not hold back Bank Data, during a dispute; unpaid undisputed charges are handled only under the termination clause (counsel's drafting).
fallback: **Other governing law:** the Supplier's home law or a neutral common-law system such as English or Singapore law (market practice). Only with a recorded rationale and, for a material outsourcing or Critical Service, a local-law opinion that the Regulator access, audit, confidentiality, location and exit clauses are enforceable under it.

**Neutral seat:** arbitration seated outside Hong Kong in a New York Convention state (market practice). Only if the Regulator carve-out survives and the Bank can still seek urgent relief in any court.

**Tiered process:** a short escalation step before proceedings, for example [20] Business Days of senior-level negotiation. Only if urgent relief and regulatory matters are carved out (counsel's drafting).
redLines: **Regulatory terms must work:** for a material outsourcing or Critical Service, sign only after a local-law opinion confirms that neither a foreign governing law nor the law where the Supplier is incorporated or the data sits defeats the Regulator access, audit, confidentiality and exit terms; otherwise, a recorded Legal review (Digital Bank Guideline para 23).

**Nothing blocks the Regulator:** no forum, arbitration confidentiality or dispute step may restrict disclosure to, or cooperation with, a Regulator, or the Bank's compliance with Applicable Law. The outsourcing should not impede HKMA access (SA-2 2.8.2), and the MA must be satisfied his powers are not hindered (Digital Bank Guideline para 23).
model: (a) This Agreement, every document it incorporates by reference, and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with any of them or their formation, including any non-contractual dispute or claim, are governed by the law of Hong Kong. This clause prevails over any other choice of law or forum in an incorporated document.

(b) [Option A: The courts of Hong Kong have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any such dispute.] [Option B: Any such dispute shall be finally resolved by arbitration seated in Hong Kong under the [HKIAC Administered Arbitration Rules] in force when the arbitration starts, before [three] arbitrators, in English.]
(c) Nothing in this clause prevents the Bank from seeking urgent injunctive or other interim relief from any court of competent jurisdiction.

(d) The Supplier irrevocably appoints [name], of [Hong Kong address], to receive service of process in any proceedings in Hong Kong. If that appointment ends, the Supplier shall appoint a replacement in Hong Kong within [10] Business Days and notify the Bank.

(e) Pending resolution of any dispute, the Supplier shall continue to perform the Services in full and shall not suspend them or withhold Bank Data. Non-payment of undisputed charges is dealt with only under [the termination clause]. No dispute resolution step, and no confidentiality obligation attaching to any proceedings, restricts either party from disclosing information to, or cooperating with, a Regulator, or the Bank from complying with Applicable Law.

(f) The Supplier warrants that, having taken appropriate advice, it knows of nothing in the governing law, the law of the place of incorporation of the Supplier or of any member of its group that can access Bank Data, or the law of any Approved Country, that would prevent it performing clauses [Regulator access, audit, confidentiality, location and exit], and shall notify the Bank promptly if that changes.
watchFor: **Home-law default:** standard terms choosing the Supplier's home law and courts, often with no Hong Kong process agent. This triggers the legal-opinion route in the fallback.

**Local law excuses performance:** a general clause making the Supplier's obligations 'subject to' its local laws, without the notice and exit mechanics in the overseas-authorities and location clauses.

**Split law through linked terms:** the signed agreement chooses Hong Kong law, but online service terms, a data processing addendum or an acceptable-use policy it incorporates choose another law or forum and prevail on conflict (third-party rights: see the HKMA access clause).
**Suspension during disputes:** a right to suspend the Services, or hold back Bank Data, while a dispute, including a fee dispute, is pending (see the exit clause for termination rights).

pushback.says: Group policy requires our home law for all customer contracts.
pushback.reply: SA-2 2.9.1 says an overseas outsourcing agreement should preferably be governed by Hong Kong law. If your law is unavoidable, we need a recorded rationale, a Hong Kong or neutral forum and, for material services, a local-law opinion that the regulatory clauses are enforceable under it.

pushback.says: We prefer arbitration to the Hong Kong courts.
pushback.reply: We can agree arbitration seated in Hong Kong, provided we can still seek urgent relief in court and the arbitration's confidentiality never stops disclosure to the Regulator.

pushback.says: We need to be able to suspend service if a fee is disputed.
pushback.reply: We will keep paying undisputed charges, and undisputed non-payment is dealt with under the termination clause after notice. Suspending service or holding back data mid-dispute would hit our customers and possibly critical operations, so we cannot accept it.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: for a material outsourcing or Critical Service, the Head of Legal approves any non-Hong Kong governing law or forum, with the rationale and legal opinion on file, and involves the CRO; for other offshore contracts, a recorded Legal review of the governing law and forum is enough.

terms.title: Termination, exit and data return
terms.summary: The bank should be able to leave: get its customer data back or destroyed (SA-2 2.5.4), move the service elsewhere (2.7.3), and do so if the HKMA, in extreme cases, requires alternative arrangements (1.3.5).
require: **Data at the end:** when the agreement ends, for whatever reason, all customer data is retrieved from the vendor or destroyed (SA-2 2.5.4).

**Regulator-required change:** a right to terminate or move the service, without penalty, if the HKMA requires alternative arrangements for the outsourced activity. The HKMA reserves that power in extreme cases where deficiencies are not rectified (SA-2 1.3.5) and, for overseas outsourcing, where overseas authorities' access to customer data seems unwarranted (2.9.1). The clause is inference from that reserved power; SA-2 does not itself require it.

**Exit plan support:** in building a viable contingency plan, SA-2 says the bank should consider whether alternative providers are available or the service could be brought back in-house in an emergency, and the costs, time and resources involved (2.7.3). For critical outsourced technology services, TM-G-1 says the bank should have a contingency plan, which may include an exit management plan and alternate providers (7.1.1). Exit management and transition assistance clauses are what make either workable (counsel's drafting).

**Mission-critical software packages:** the bank may consider including an escrow agreement in the contract, giving access to the source code in defined circumstances such as the vendor ceasing business (TM-G-1 4.2.6; permissive, 'may consider').

**Exit strategy for critical operations:** where the vendor supports critical operations, the bank should have business continuity and contingency procedures and exit strategies that keep it operationally resilient if the vendor fails or is disrupted, and should not continue an arrangement that may weaken the resilience of its critical operations (OR-2 6.2).

sources.label: SPM OR-2 Operational resilience
sources.note: Non-statutory guidance note; V.1, 31 May 2022 (the final module you supplied).

sources.label: Digital Bank Guideline
sources.note: Issued under s.16(10) of the Banking Ordinance, not s.7(3).

drafting: **Continuity during exit:** the vendor keeps providing the service on existing terms through a defined transition period.

**Resolution and s.52:** add that the vendor may not terminate or suspend merely because the MA exercises powers under the Banking Ordinance, in particular s.52 (inference from Digital Bank Guideline para 23, under which the MA must be satisfied that those powers 'will not be hindered by the outsourcing arrangements'). Separately, as counsel's drafting not drawn from para 23, add that the vendor may not terminate or suspend merely because the bank enters recovery or resolution, and that the contract can transfer to a successor (see Stage 10).
terms.cloud: Check exit is practical: data export formats, egress costs and timing, and deletion certificates at the end.

playbook.why: Most of the clause rests on SA-2 and TM-G-1 guidance (2.5.4, 2.7.3, 7.1.1), but two parts are floors: the MA must be satisfied that outsourcing will not hinder his powers, in particular s.52 (Digital Bank Guideline para 23, a statutory guideline), and the PDPO requires contractual or other means against over-retention of Personal Data by a processor (DPP2(3)).
preferred: **Bank's exit rights:** termination for convenience on [6] months' notice, and without termination charge for material breach, insolvency, persistent service failure (see the service levels clause) or where a Regulator requires alternative arrangements (SA-2 1.3.5, 2.9.1); change of control is covered in the change-control clause.

**Supplier's exit limited:** the Supplier may not suspend the Services, and may terminate only for non-payment of undisputed charges after notice and escalation, on [three] months' notice followed by the full Exit Period (counsel's drafting).

**Exit Period and plan:** an exit plan delivered soon after signing and tested; on any termination or expiry, the Services continue on existing terms for an Exit Period of up to [18] months, with help to transfer to the Bank or a replacement supplier (SA-2 2.7.3; TM-G-1 7.1.1; OR-2 6.2).

**Data back, then deleted:** Bank Data returned in an agreed usable format and, once the Bank confirms it has a complete copy, deleted from all systems, Subcontractors and backups with a certificate (SA-2 2.5.4; PDPO DPP2(3)); escrow, where the Bank decides it is needed, for mission-critical software (TM-G-1 4.2.6).
fallback: **Shorter Exit Period:** acceptable for non-critical Services if it is long enough to migrate under the Bank's exit plan and the Supplier cannot end it early while charges are paid.

**Charges on exit:** charges for exit assistance beyond continued Services, or for convenience termination, are acceptable only at rates or on a declining schedule fixed in advance, and never on termination for regulatory reasons, breach, insolvency, change of control or persistent failure, or under the Bank's business exit plan.
**Backups on rotation:** erasing backup copies on the Supplier's normal cycle is acceptable if that is within [90] days and the copies stay protected, confidential and unused meanwhile.

**Wider Supplier grounds:** Supplier termination for the Bank's material breach of licence or use restrictions, or where continuing would be unlawful (for example under sanctions), is acceptable only on the longest notice the law allows, then the Exit Period so far as lawful, never for Regulator action or resolution.
redLines: **Regulator powers and resolution:** no Supplier termination, suspension or change of the Services because the MA exercises Banking Ordinance powers, in particular s.52 (Digital Bank Guideline para 23); resolution measures alone cannot trigger termination either while the Bank performs (Cap. 628 s.89).

**Personal Data not kept:** the Supplier must not keep Personal Data it processes for the Bank longer than the processing needs, including after exit; the PDPO requires contractual or other means, a contract being the usual one (PDPO DPP2(3)). SA-2 adds return or destruction at the end (2.5.4).
model: (a) The Bank may terminate this Agreement in whole or part: (i) for convenience on [6] months' notice; or (ii) by notice taking effect when it specifies, without termination charge or other liability, if a Regulator requires alternative arrangements for any of the Services, the Supplier becomes insolvent, or the Supplier commits a material breach that cannot be remedied or [is not remedied within [30] days] after notice.

(b) The Supplier shall not suspend the Services for any reason [except so far as strictly necessary to contain an Incident, with immediate notice]. It may terminate only if the Bank fails to pay undisputed charges within [60] days after a final written notice escalated to [the Bank's chief operating officer], and then on [three] months' notice, after which paragraph (d) applies [with Exit Period charges payable monthly in advance].

(c) The Supplier shall not terminate, suspend or change the Services because a Regulator exercises any supervisory, regulatory or resolution power in relation to the Bank (including under section 52 of the Banking Ordinance), or because the Bank implements its business exit plan, so long as the Bank continues to pay undisputed charges.

(d) The Supplier shall deliver an exit plan within [90] days after signing, keep it updated as the Bank approves and, for Critical Services, test it with the Bank [every [two] years]. On any termination or expiry, however arising, the Supplier shall continue the Services on the terms of this Agreement for an Exit Period of [up to [18] months] as the Bank specifies, giving the planned transition assistance and cooperating with any replacement supplier.

(e) The Supplier shall return all Bank Data in [the agreed format] within [30] days after the Bank's request and at the end of the Exit Period. Once the Bank confirms it holds a complete, usable copy, the Supplier shall securely delete all Bank Data held by it or any Subcontractor within [30] days (backups within the cycle in clause [Personal data]) and certify deletion. Copies Applicable Law requires it to keep stay confidential and are deleted when no longer required.

(f) For [the software listed in Schedule 9], the Supplier shall deposit with [escrow agent] the source code, build and deployment scripts and documentation [and, for hosted software, what is needed to run the production environment], releasable to the Bank if the Supplier ceases business, becomes insolvent, stops supporting the software or fails to continue the Services during the Exit Period. It shall update the deposit at each major release.
watchFor: **Supplier walk-away:** a short Supplier right to terminate for convenience, or on vague 'regulatory or reputational' grounds, leaving a Critical Service without time to migrate.

**Regulatory triggers:** termination or suspension rights on the Bank's 'change in regulatory status', 'regulatory intervention' or 'any insolvency or analogous event', which would catch s.52 action, resolution, or the exit plan a digital bank must have (Digital Bank Guideline para 20).

**Data held back:** return of Bank Data conditional on payment of all sums claimed, export only in a proprietary format, automatic deletion before the Bank has its copy, or deletion 'within a commercially reasonable time' with no certificate.

**Exit help by agreement:** transition assistance only 'as mutually agreed', at then-current rates or only after termination by the Bank, with no duty to keep the Services running after termination or expiry (see the continuity clause).

pushback.says: We can't keep providing the service for 18 months after termination; termination means termination.
pushback.reply: You are paid throughout. SA-2 expects our contingency plan to consider moving to another provider or back in-house, and the time and cost involved (2.7.3), and OR-2 expects exit strategies for critical operations (6.2). Without an Exit Period, termination itself becomes the disruption.

pushback.says: If a regulator takes control of your bank, we need the right to walk away.
pushback.reply: This one is a must-have. The MA must be satisfied that the outsourcing will not hinder his powers, in particular s.52 (Digital Bank Guideline para 23), and resolution measures do not by themselves trigger termination anyway (Cap. 628 s.89). You will still be paid.

pushback.says: Our backups are kept for a year and we can't delete selectively.
pushback.reply: This is a must-have. Tell us the rotation period: backups can roll off on your normal cycle within [90] days, encrypted, confidential and unused meanwhile, but not a year. The PDPO requires contractual or other means so Personal Data is not kept longer than necessary (PDPO DPP2(3)), and SA-2 expects customer data retrieved or destroyed at the end (2.5.4).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: a red-line deviation to the Head of Legal and the CRO, who should consider whether the arrangement can proceed and, for a material outsourcing, whether to discuss it with the HKMA; other deviations to the outsourcing committee.

terms.title: Intragroup services
terms.summary: Services from a parent or affiliate are still outsourcing (SA-2 1.1.1). Being in the group earns no discount: whether or not the provider is in the group, the MA must be satisfied that the outsourced operations keep adequate security controls, that customer confidentiality and the PDPO are respected, and that his Banking Ordinance powers, in particular s.52, are not hindered (Digital Bank Guideline para 23). Responsibilities should be set out in writing. The bank is a separate legal entity: its directors are not absolved from responsibility for the effects of group policies and actions applied to it, and its board remains ultimately responsible for their implementation and effectiveness in the bank (CG-1 V.4 9.2.2).
require: **Form:** SA-2 expects a service agreement (2.4.1). A memorandum of understanding 'may be acceptable' where the provider is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the bank, or the head office or another branch of a foreign bank (2.4.3). A tech-group parent or sister company falls outside 2.4.3, so use a full agreement (inference from 2.4.1 and 2.4.3).

**Documented responsibilities:** senior management should ensure the respective responsibilities of the bank and group offices for IT controls and support are clearly set out (TM-G-1 2.6.1, written for overseas offices of the same banking group, where policies, procedures or service agreements may serve). For a non-bank group affiliate, put them in the service agreement (inference from SA-2 2.4.1 and 2.4.3).

**Same standard:** the bank should manage dependencies on intragroup entities as it would outsourcing arrangements. Before entering into an intragroup arrangement that supports critical operations, it should verify whether the group entity has at least an equivalent level of operational resilience or, where that is not feasible, take other steps to satisfy itself that the arrangement will not weaken its ability to deliver critical operations in a disruption. It should not enter into or continue one that may weaken that resilience (OR-2 6.2).

sources.label: SPM OR-2 Operational resilience
sources.note: Non-statutory guidance note; V.1, 31 May 2022 (the final module you supplied).

sources.label: Digital Bank Guideline
sources.note: Issued under s.16(10) of the Banking Ordinance (authorization guideline), not s.7(3). The MA does not object in principle to outsourcing to a provider that may or may not be part of the group owning the digital bank, but material outsourcing should be discussed with the MA in advance and SA-2 compliance demonstrated (para 23).

sources.label: SPM CG-1 Corporate governance
sources.note: Checked against V.4 (1 August 2025). Section 9.2 covers any AI that belongs to a larger group of companies, so it applies directly to a digital bank in a technology group, not by analogy (see also Digital Bank Guideline paras 8, 11). Key policies may be set centrally at holding company level (9.2.1), but the directors are not absolved from responsibility for the effects of policies applied to the bank, 'group' policy or not, and the board stays ultimately responsible for their implementation and effectiveness (9.2.2). The board should give input to, or promptly evaluate, group policies. If one may breach legal or regulatory requirements or harm the bank's sound and prudent operation, or the holding company does not respond adequately to the board's concerns, the board should record its dissent, act to protect the bank, and consider independent advice and raising the issue with the HKMA (9.2.3). CG-1 also lists the parent company among relationships that can create conflicts of interest (2.6.11), and expects a board-level conflicts policy (2.6.14). For directors appointed by a controlling shareholder, the board should consider set procedures or regular reviews to confirm they act in the bank's best interest (2.6.15). V.4 adds that the chief executive and alternates should avoid directorships or management posts outside the bank's banking group unless they can satisfy the board on conflicts and time (2.6.13); a role at a non-bank parent that supplies the services may be one (inference). V.1 had the group points at 6.2.13–6.2.14, framed for subsidiaries of banking institutions.

drafting: **Arm's length:** price and terms that would stand up as commercial, and the same HKMA-access, audit and exit terms as a third-party contract.

playbook.why: The Digital Bank Guideline, a statutory guideline under BO s.16(10), applies its outsourcing conditions whether or not the provider is in the group, including points the MA must be satisfied of (para 23); CG-1 V.4 9.2.2 (statutory guideline) keeps the bank's board ultimately responsible for group policies and practices applied to the bank. Document form and the resilience check are SA-2 and OR-2 expectations, tradeable above that floor.
preferred: **Full agreement:** a written services agreement with the same Regulator access, audit, confidentiality, data, continuity and exit terms as a third-party contract (SA-2 1.1.1, 2.4.1). A memorandum of understanding fits only a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Bank (SA-2 2.4.3).

**Responsibilities mapped:** a schedule allocating responsibility between the Bank and the group Supplier for each IT control and support activity, reviewed at least [annually] (by analogy with TM-G-1 2.6.1, written for offices of the same banking group).

**Resilience verified:** before the arrangement supports critical operations, evidence, measured against agreed recovery objectives, that the group Supplier's operational resilience is at least equivalent to the Bank's, or other steps where that is not feasible, then ongoing information to keep checking it (OR-2 6.2; see the continuity clause).

**Arm's length and independent:** commercial pricing and service levels (counsel's drafting), and the Bank's rights exercisable by its own board and management without group approval (inference from CG-1 V.4 9.2.2–9.2.3).
fallback: **Group master agreement:** a group-wide master agreement with a Bank schedule. Only if the schedule prevails on regulatory terms and the Bank can vary or terminate its schedule by its own decision.

**Group frameworks:** reliance on the group's security, continuity or resilience framework. Only if it meets the Bank's own requirements and the Bank keeps information and testing rights; for operational resilience, it must let the Bank materially fulfil OR-2's objectives and requirements, discussed with the HKMA in advance (OR-2 2.4, footnote 3).

**Group assurance:** group internal audit or group-appointed assessors for routine assurance. Only if they are independent of those running the service, can report directly to the Bank's board, and the Bank's and the Regulator's own rights stay intact (cf. TM-E-1 3.3.1(iii); see the audit clause).

**Calibrated liability:** a lower cap than a third party would accept. Only if confidentiality, data and regulatory-cooperation breaches stay outside it and the board records why (see the liability clause).
redLines: **No regulatory discount:** the group Supplier accepts the security, confidentiality and PDPO terms in full, and nothing may hinder the MA's powers, including s.52 (Digital Bank Guideline para 23). BO ss.55–56 do not reach a parent or sister company, and s.63(2A) gives only an information power, so inspection rights must come from the contract (SA-2 2.8.2).

**No group override:** the Bank's rights to audit, instruct, suspend, terminate or exit must not depend on group policy, a group committee or parent consent, in the contract or in the Bank's articles, shareholder agreement or group authority matrix (inference from the board's duty to protect the bank, CG-1 V.4 9.2.2–9.2.3).
model: (a) The Supplier's membership of the Bank's group does not limit or qualify any of its obligations under this Agreement, including on Regulator access, audit, confidentiality, Personal Data, data location, continuity and exit. No group policy, intragroup arrangement or instruction from another group member prevails over this Agreement. No group member may use Bank Data for its own purposes except under a separate written agreement the Bank approves and Applicable Law permits.

(b) [Schedule R] allocates responsibility between the Bank and the Supplier for each IT control, support activity and other process used to provide the Services. The parties shall review [Schedule R] at least [annually] and on any material change to the Services or to either party's organisation.

(c) The Bank may exercise any right under this Agreement, including to audit, instruct, suspend and terminate, by decision of its own board or management. No such exercise needs the consent of, or consultation with, any other member of the Bank's group.

(d) Before any Critical Service goes live, and at least [annually] after that, the Supplier shall give the Bank evidence, including test results, that it can deliver each Critical Service within the recovery commitments in [Schedule 3, Part B], which reflect the Bank's tolerances for disruption [or, where the Bank agrees that is not feasible, other evidence it accepts in writing], and shall tell the Bank promptly of anything that may materially reduce its resilience.

(e) The charges and other terms of this Agreement are set on an arm's length basis. On request, the Supplier shall give the Bank the information it reasonably needs to demonstrate this to its board, its auditors or any Regulator.

(f) If the Supplier ceases to be a member of the Bank's group, this Agreement continues on its terms and is not terminated or repriced for that reason. The Bank may, [within [12] months after that,] terminate it in whole or in part on [three] months' notice without any termination charge or other liability, with exit assistance under clause [exit].
watchFor: **Lighter paperwork:** an MoU, group policy or cost-sharing agreement in place of a services agreement with a parent or sister company, or a services agreement with mutual claim waivers, nominal caps and no service levels (SA-2 2.4.1, 2.4.3; see the liability clause).
**Group override:** the Bank's rights made subject to group policy, group IT standards 'as amended from time to time' or approval by a group committee.

**Group use of data:** rights in the services agreement for the Supplier or other group members to use Customer Data for their own analytics, product development or cross-selling. A group member doing so is not a data processor (PDPO s.2(12), DPP2(4)); such use needs prescribed consent (DPP3) and, for direct marketing, written consent (s.35J; CoBP 8.3(d)).

**Exit on separation:** automatic termination, repricing or a Supplier termination right if the Bank leaves the group, is sold or enters resolution, which strands Critical Services exactly when continuity matters most (see the exit clause).

pushback.says: We are your parent; the HKMA can come to us anyway, so access and audit clauses are unnecessary.
pushback.reply: This is a must-have. Para 23 of the Digital Bank Guideline applies the same outsourcing conditions whether or not the provider is in the group. BO s.63(2A) lets the HKMA ask you for information, but its examination powers under BO ss.55–56 reach the Bank and its subsidiaries, not you, so inspection rights must be in the contract.

pushback.says: Group policy already sets these standards for every subsidiary.
pushback.reply: We can align with group standards, but our directors are not absolved by group policy and our board stays ultimately responsible (CG-1 V.4 9.2.2). Our contractual rights cannot depend on group approval.

pushback.says: A full arm's-length contract is excessive inside one group.
pushback.reply: SA-2 treats group providers as outsourcing (1.1.1) and expects a service agreement (2.4.1); an MoU fits only a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Bank (2.4.3). We can start from your group template with a Bank schedule.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: deviations go to the Head of Legal and the CRO, then to the board or its risk committee, with directors appointed by or connected to the Supplier's group declaring the interest and abstaining under the board's conflicts policy (CG-1 V.4 2.6.14–2.6.15).

terms.title: Onboarding, screening and monitoring vendors (AML)
terms.summary: eKYC, screening and transaction-monitoring vendors do part of the bank's AML work, but the bank keeps the legal duty. The AML Guideline treats every 'should' as mandatory (para 1.6).
require: **Bank's procedures:** a vendor or agent that applies CDD on the bank's behalf, following the bank's procedures and under the bank's control of their effective implementation, is an outsourcing or agency arrangement rather than reliance on an intermediary (4.11.2), and the bank remains liable for any CDD failure (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(6)). Binding the vendor to the bank's CDD procedures and giving the bank control rights follows from this (drafting inference).

**Records wherever held:** wherever CDD and transaction records are held, including by a vendor, a group entity or offshore, the bank must comply with Hong Kong requirements, especially Part 3 of AMLO Schedule 2 (8.9). CDD records: the whole relationship plus at least five years after it ends (8.3–8.4); transaction records: at least five years after the transaction is completed, whether or not the relationship has ended (8.5–8.6); kept as originals or as copies on microfilm or in a computer database (8.7); longer where the HKMA requires it by written notice (8.8).

**Swift access:** all CDD information and transaction records available swiftly to the HKMA, other authorities and auditors upon appropriate authority (8.2(b)). Senior management should also, as far as practicable, ensure the Compliance Officer and MLRO can access all available information, including CDD records, on a timely basis (3.8(g)); applying this to records a vendor holds is counsel's inference.

**Screening data:** if the bank subscribes to a third-party database of terrorists and designated parties, it must take appropriate measures, such as periodic sample testing, to ensure the database is complete and accurate (6.13). UN Security Council designations go in as soon as practicable after promulgation, whether or not implemented in Hong Kong (6.14); the database includes the Gazette, CEDB and HKMA-circulated lists and is updated whenever they change (6.15); and the bank keeps ultimate responsibility even where its overseas office maintains the database or does the screening (6.19).

**Monitoring systems:** the bank must regularly review its transaction monitoring systems, and the parameters and thresholds must be properly documented and independently validated (5.8). Where the system is a vendor's, the contract needs to give the bank enough documentation and transparency to do this (drafting inference; 5.8 does not mention vendors).
**Remote onboarding:** supplementary verification technology must guard against impersonation, and the bank must be able to show the HKMA that it does (4.10.4).

sources.label: HKMA AML/CFT Guideline
sources.note: Issued under s.7 AMLO and s.7(3) of the Banking Ordinance; revised May 2023 (the version you supplied).

sources.label: AMLO (Cap. 615)
sources.note: CDD by an agent leaves the bank liable (s.18(6)); duty to keep records and the manner of keeping them (ss.20–21). The CDD and record-keeping duties are specified provisions: breach can lead to disciplinary action, and a knowing breach is an offence (ss.5(5), 5(11), 21).

drafting: **Legal holds:** the vendor keeps records longer on the bank's instruction and never deletes them during a hold.
**Tipping-off:** bind vendors that see alerts, case files or report information to confidentiality covering suspicions, since disclosing them can be an offence (7.6).
**Exit:** all CDD and screening records handed back in usable form before the vendor stops.

playbook.why: The AML/CFT Guideline is a statutory guideline in which every 'should' is mandatory (AML Guideline 1.6), and the AMLO keeps CDD and record-keeping duties with the bank even when an agent does the work (AMLO Sch. 2 ss.18(6), 20–21). Those duties are specified provisions: contravening them can lead to disciplinary action, and a knowing contravention is an offence (AMLO ss.5(5), 5(11), 21).
preferred: **Bank's procedures, bank's control:** the vendor applies the bank's CDD and screening procedures as amended from time to time, and the bank can direct, test and change their implementation, so the arrangement stays an outsourcing, not reliance (AML Guideline 4.11.2; AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(6)).

**Statutory retention:** CDD records, account files and business correspondence kept for the relationship plus five years, and transaction records for five years after completion, longer under a bank hold or Regulator notice, and deleted only once the bank confirms it holds a complete copy (AMLO Sch. 2 ss.20–21; AML Guideline 8.3–8.8).

**Transparent tools:** for screening, new and amended UN designations loaded as soon as practicable, other lists updated whenever they change, and bank sample testing at any time; for monitoring, full documentation of rules, parameters and thresholds delivered to the bank for review and independent validation (AML Guideline 5.8, 6.13–6.15).

**Evidence for the HKMA:** for remote onboarding, test results, performance data and methodology sufficient for the bank to demonstrate to the HKMA that its supplementary measures guard against impersonation (AML Guideline 4.10.4).
fallback: **Records held by the vendor:** accept the vendor keeping the long-term AMLO archive instead of the bank holding its own copy, only if the records clause's access terms are met, the bank can retrieve any record swiftly in usable form, and the statutory periods and holds bind the vendor wherever the records sit (AML Guideline 8.2(b), 8.9).

**Proprietary models:** accept a logic summary and a full parameter and threshold register instead of full model documentation, disclosed under confidentiality to named bank compliance staff, including the MLRO, and the bank's independent validator, only if the bank can review the settings and the validator can test them against its operations (AML Guideline 3.8(g), 5.8).

**Database testing:** accept bank-run sample tests at agreed intervals plus the vendor's own list-reconciliation reports instead of testing at any time, only if gaps found are corrected and reported promptly (AML Guideline 6.13).

**Standard multi-client terms:** a pooled screening or eKYC service may keep its standard terms, only if a bank-specific addendum that prevails over them adds every red-line term in this clause (control of any CDD it performs, testing, retention and holds, retrieval, list updates, model documentation and HKMA evidence) and the tipping-off term.
redLines: **Control and retrieval:** where the vendor performs CDD and is not relied on as an intermediary, the bank must control implementation of its procedures (AML Guideline 4.11.2; AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(6)). Every AML vendor must let the bank obtain the CDD and transaction records it holds swiftly for the HKMA, other authorities and auditors (AML Guideline 8.2(b)).

**Retention floor:** no deletion while a Regulator notice or bank hold applies, and none before the AMLO periods end unless the bank has confirmed it holds a complete, readable copy kept as the AMLO requires (AMLO Sch. 2 ss.20–21; AML Guideline 8.8–8.9).

**No black box:** the bank must be able to test the screening database, review monitoring parameters and thresholds itself and have them documented and independently validated, and demonstrate to the HKMA that remote verification guards against impersonation (AML Guideline 4.10.4, 5.8, 6.13).
model: (a) The Supplier shall perform any Services comprising customer due diligence, screening or transaction monitoring only under the Bank's written procedures as amended from time to time, implementing each change the Bank directs within [10] Business Days or, if it needs development, the period agreed under [the change control clause], and always within any period Applicable Law requires. The Bank controls, and may test at any time, the Supplier's implementation of them.

(b) Subject to paragraph (c), the Supplier shall keep, in the manner Applicable Law requires, each record it holds that the Bank must keep, until the earlier of: (i) the Bank's written confirmation that it holds a complete, readable copy; and (ii) five years after the transaction completes or, for due diligence records, account files and correspondence, after the relationship end date the Bank notifies, or any longer period the Bank notifies.

(c) The Supplier shall not delete or alter any record under a hold the Bank notifies. It shall deliver any record the Bank requests, to the Bank or as it directs to the Regulator or its auditors, within the times in [the records clause], treating a request the Bank links to law enforcement as a Regulator request, and give the Bank a complete copy of all such records before any Exit Period ends.

(d) Where the Services include a screening database, the Supplier shall reflect each new, amended or removed United Nations Security Council designation [within [24] hours] after promulgation, whether or not given effect in Hong Kong, update the lists in [Schedule [ ] (Sanctions Lists)] [within [1] Business Day] after each change, and support the Bank's sample testing of the database [at any time], correcting any gap found [within [1] Business Day].

(e) Where the Services include transaction monitoring or remote identity verification, the Supplier shall document its rules, parameters, thresholds and models, give the Bank that documentation, and change them only under [the change control clause], with test results before go-live or, for an urgent fix, [within [1] Business Day] afterwards. It shall give the Bank and its validator what they need to validate them and, for remote verification, show the Regulator it guards against impersonation.

(f) The Supplier shall promptly tell the Bank of any sign of fraud, impersonation, money laundering, terrorist financing or sanctions evasion it detects concerning the Services or the Bank's customers. It shall keep each such sign, alert, case file or internal report confidential, and ensure its personnel and Subcontractors disclose none of them to anyone but the Bank. Nothing in this Agreement restricts a disclosure Applicable Law requires or permits, including to an authorized officer.
watchFor: **Retention by vendor policy:** a clause letting the vendor delete data on its own schedule or after a short fixed period, before the bank confirms it holds a complete copy or despite a bank hold. See also the data processor clause on retention.

**Black-box models:** wording that treats rules, thresholds or match logic as trade secrets the bank cannot see or have validated, or lets the vendor retune them without the bank's approval and testing (AML Guideline 5.8). See the change-control clause.

**'As is' lists:** list data supplied 'as is' with no commitment to completeness or accuracy, updated only 'periodically' or on the vendor's release cycle, or covering only sanctions given effect in Hong Kong (AML Guideline 6.13–6.15).

**Reliance language:** drafting that says the vendor uses its own procedures or acts as the bank's 'intermediary'. If that is the real model, use the intermediary clause; if not, delete it (AML Guideline 4.11.2).

pushback.says: Our platform is standardised across clients; we cannot keep bespoke retention periods for one bank.
pushback.reply: The periods are statutory (AMLO Sch. 2 s.20) and apply wherever the records are held (AML Guideline 8.9). This is a must-have. If your platform cannot hold them, stream the records to us so we keep them, and delete only on our instruction.

pushback.says: Our thresholds and models are proprietary; we will not disclose them.
pushback.reply: We must regularly review our own parameters and thresholds and have them documented and independently validated (AML Guideline 5.8), and that is mandatory. We can limit disclosure to named compliance staff and a named validator under confidentiality, but the bank must see them. We cannot accept a refusal.

pushback.says: We only supply a tool; AML compliance is the bank's responsibility, not ours.
pushback.reply: Agreed that the bank stays liable (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(6)). That is why we need control, records and evidence from you: without them we cannot meet duties the law leaves with us.

playbook.escalate: Suggest the MLRO and Head of Compliance, with Head of Legal, sign off any deviation, and that a refused red line goes to the CRO, with a discussion with the HKMA considered where the outsourcing is material.

terms.title: Relying on an intermediary for CDD
terms.summary: Reliance is a separate regime: a regulated intermediary performs part of CDD with its own procedures, and the bank should obtain confirmations and undertakings that secure access to what it collected (4.11.3–4.11.5). The bank keeps ultimate responsibility (4.11.1).
require: **Eligible intermediary:** only the categories in AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(3) qualify, and the bank must take appropriate measures to confirm the intermediary meets the criteria (4.11.8–4.11.14).
**Written confirmation:** the intermediary agrees to act as the bank's intermediary and states which CDD measures it will perform (4.11.3(a)).
**Data straight away:** the bank obtains the data or information immediately after each CDD measure; copies of documents can follow (4.11.4).
**Documents on request:** copies of documents and records provided on request without delay, throughout the record-keeping period (4.11.3(b), 4.11.5).

**Retention undertaking:** where the intermediary keeps the documents and records, an undertaking to keep all underlying CDD information for the whole relationship and at least five years after it ends, or for any longer period the HKMA specifies (4.11.5).
**On exit or failure:** hand over all CDD information if the intermediary is about to cease trading or stops acting for the bank (4.11.5, 4.11.7, 8.12).
**Ongoing monitoring stays with the bank:** reliance does not cover it (4.11.1, footnote 48).
**Record-keeping systems:** the intermediary has systems to comply with all AMLO and Guideline record-keeping requirements (8.10).
**Doubts:** if the bank doubts the intermediary's reliability, it reviews the intermediary's ability to perform CDD and redoes doubtful CDD as soon as reasonably practicable (4.11.7).

sources.label: AMLO (Cap. 615)
sources.note: Conditions for carrying out CDD by means of intermediaries.

drafting: **Test it:** the bank should sample-test that documents arrive on demand without undue delay (4.11.6); give it the right to.

playbook.why: AMLO Sch. 2 s.18 makes written consent and on-request delivery of CDD records conditions of reliance, and s.18(4) is a specified provision: breach can lead to disciplinary action, and a knowing breach is an offence (AMLO ss.5(5), 5(11), 21). The AML/CFT Guideline, a statutory guideline, adds mandatory confirmations and undertakings (AML Guideline 1.6, 4.11.3–4.11.5).
preferred: **Written consent and scope:** the intermediary consents in writing to act as the bank's intermediary and lists each CDD measure it performs, by customer type or product (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(1)(a); AML Guideline 4.11.3(a)).

**Data at once, documents on demand:** CDD data and information passed to the bank immediately after each measure, and copies of documents or records provided without delay on request, within a fixed number of Business Days (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(1)(b), (4); AML Guideline 4.11.4).

**Retention and hand-over:** all underlying CDD information kept for the bank's relationship plus at least five years, counted from the bank's notice that it has ended, or longer if the HKMA specifies, and handed over if the intermediary is about to cease trading or stops acting for the bank (AML Guideline 4.11.5, 8.12).

**Eligibility facts and testing:** warranties of the facts that make it eligible under AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(3), including that no local law blocks delivery, prompt notice of any change, and rights to sample-test retrieval and review its AML/CFT policies (AML Guideline 4.11.6, 4.11.9, 4.11.11).
fallback: **Group reliance:** for a related foreign financial institution, accept a group policy or intragroup memorandum instead of a bilateral contract, only if it contains the consent and every undertaking, group-level supervision is shown, and the bank takes reasonable measures to mitigate the ML/TF risk, including country risk (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(3A), (4)(c); AML Guideline 4.11.12–4.11.14).
**Intermediary's own form:** accept its standard reliance letter instead of the bank's form, only if it covers every element of AML Guideline 4.11.3–4.11.5 and 8.12; fill any gap by side letter.

**Electronic copies:** accept certified electronic copies or system extracts instead of paper copies, only if the records are kept as originals or as copies on microfilm or a computer database and are readable on delivery (AMLO Sch. 2 s.21).

**Desk-based oversight:** accept regular sample retrieval tests and review of its AML/CFT policies instead of on-site audit, only if a failed test triggers the bank's review of the intermediary's reliability (AML Guideline 4.11.6–4.11.7).
redLines: **Statutory conditions:** no reliance without the intermediary's written consent and the bank being satisfied that copies come without delay on request, and none on anyone outside the AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(3) categories (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(1), (3)).

**Undertakings:** do not sign without immediate transfer of CDD data after each measure, the retention undertaking and the hand-over undertaking on ceasing to trade or to act (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(4)(a); AML Guideline 4.11.5).
**Ongoing monitoring stays with the bank:** no term that treats the intermediary as monitoring the business relationship for the bank; reliance cannot cover it (AML Guideline 4.11.1, footnote 48).
model: (a) The Supplier consents to act as the Bank's intermediary under section 18 of Schedule 2 to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) and shall perform, applying its own procedures, for each customer it introduces to the Bank or the Bank refers to it under this Agreement, the customer due diligence measures listed in [Schedule [ ] (Due Diligence Measures)] and no others.

(b) Immediately after performing each such measure, the Supplier shall give the Bank all data and information it obtained in doing so through [the agreed secure channel]. On the Bank's request at any time before the period in paragraph (c) ends, the Supplier shall provide a copy of any document, or a record of any data or information, so obtained without delay and in any event within [2] Business Days.

(c) The Supplier shall keep all underlying customer due diligence information for each customer within paragraph (a) throughout the Bank's relationship with that customer and for at least five years after the Bank notifies it that the relationship has ended, or any longer period the Bank notifies as specified by the Regulator, in systems meeting Applicable Law's record-keeping requirements. The Bank shall give that notice [within [30] days] after the relationship ends.

(d) If the Supplier is about to cease trading or to act as the Bank's intermediary, or this Agreement ends for any reason, the Supplier shall immediately supply the Bank with copies of all underlying customer due diligence information for every customer within paragraph (a). This paragraph and paragraphs (b) and (c) survive termination.

(e) The Supplier warrants that it is [category, supervisory authority and licence], that it has adequate measures to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing and is supervised for compliance with them, and that no law prevents it complying with paragraphs (b) to (d). It shall notify the Bank [within [2] Business Days] of any change in those facts, any material change to those measures, or any regulatory action against it concerning them.

(f) The Supplier shall respond to the sample requests and other tests the Bank makes from time to time and provide its anti-money laundering policies and procedures on request. The Supplier does not perform ongoing monitoring of any business relationship on the Bank's behalf.
watchFor: **Soft retrieval promises:** documents available on request only on a reasonable-endeavours basis or subject to the intermediary's own retention policy; the bank must be satisfied they will come without delay (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(1)(b)).

**Local-law carve-outs:** delivery of documents 'subject to' secrecy, data protection or blocking laws in the intermediary's jurisdiction, with no statement that none of them prevents prompt delivery; the bank must be satisfied copies will come without delay (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(1)(b)).

**Outsourcing in disguise:** a provider that will follow the bank's procedures under the bank's control is an outsourcing or agency, not reliance; use the AML vendors clause instead (AML Guideline 4.11.2).

**Undertakings that lapse or start late:** retention, retrieval and hand-over duties that end with the agreement, or a retention period counted from the end of the intermediary's own client relationship rather than the bank's (AML Guideline 4.11.5).

pushback.says: We are regulated ourselves and our own rules cover record-keeping, so we will not sign separate undertakings.
pushback.reply: The bank must obtain the undertakings itself (AML Guideline 4.11.5), and the statute makes your written consent and on-request delivery conditions of our reliance (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18). This is a must-have; a short reliance letter will do.

pushback.says: We send CDD data to clients monthly, not after each customer.
pushback.reply: The AMLO requires us to obtain the data immediately after each measure (Sch. 2 s.18(4)(a)). Copies of documents can follow later, but the data cannot. Without this we will do the CDD ourselves.

pushback.says: We can produce documents on request, but within 30 days.
pushback.reply: We must be satisfied that copies come without delay (AMLO Sch. 2 s.18(1)(b)) and must sample-test it (AML Guideline 4.11.6). We can agree a short fixed period in Business Days, not a month.

playbook.escalate: Suggest the MLRO approves each intermediary and any non-standard reliance terms, with Head of Legal signing off departures from the model undertakings and the CRO deciding if a red line is refused.

terms.title: Debt collection agencies
terms.summary: The Code of Banking Practice sets detailed, prescriptive terms for collection agencies, and the bank remains accountable to customers for complaints about the agency and should not disclaim responsibility for its misconduct (CoBP 46.5).
require: **Formal contract:** a formal contractual relationship, with the contract or written instructions requiring collectors to observe the conduct rules in 46.1 to 46.3 (46.4).

**Conduct:** act within the law, avoid anything prejudicial to the bank's business, integrity, reputation or goodwill, and keep a strict duty of confidentiality over customer information (46.1). Never use intimidation or violence ('must not'), and do not use harassment or improper tactics such as posters, persistent calls or electronic messages, calls at unreasonable hours, pestering referees, family or friends, false names, anonymous calls or notes, abusive or threatening remarks, or false or misleading representations (46.2).
**Third parties:** no attempt to recover from referees, family or friends who have not formally guaranteed the debt, by written instruction or contract clause (46.3).
**Principal and agent:** the contract states the relationship is principal and agent, and prohibits sub-contracting the collection to anyone else (46.5).
**Identification:** collectors identify themselves and the bank, and carry authorization documents without account details (46.10).
**Records:** customers told that calls are recorded and why; records of other contacts kept; recordings and contact records kept at least 30 days (47.5).

**Limits:** no authority to start legal proceedings without the bank's formal approval (47.9); no free hand on recovery procedures (47.3); all recovery stops immediately once the debt is settled in full (46.11), and once the bank learns of a bankruptcy order against the debtor (46.13).

**Data privacy:** clauses protecting customer information and barring sharing with anyone else, including other agencies (CoBP 47.11). An agency handling customer data only on the bank's behalf will usually be a data processor (counsel's view), so the bank must also adopt contractual or other means against excessive retention and unauthorized or accidental access, processing, erasure, loss or use (PDPO DPP2(3), DPP4(2)); see the data processor clause.

sources.label: HKMA Guideline 3.4.1 Debt Collection Agencies
sources.note: Letter of 3 May 1996: no intimidation or violence, and no recovery from non-guarantor third parties, given to agencies in writing.

sources.label: PDPO (Cap. 486)
sources.note: An agent's acts done with the bank's authority are treated as done by the bank as well as by the agent, for PDPO purposes other than criminal proceedings; this attributes liability and does not itself require any clause.

drafting: **Oversight rights:** unscheduled visits to check professionalism, integrity, training, resourcing and compliance (47.6); a duty to take remedial action on complaints (47.7); termination for unacceptable practices or breach (47.12).

**Selection file:** company search identifying owners and directors, a basic assessment of financial soundness, a site visit, an evaluation of operations and, for a new agency, references from at least two existing clients (preferably authorized institutions), with the procedures regularly reviewed (47.1).

**Data minimisation:** do not pass information about referees or any third party other than debtors and guarantors to the agency; if a referee must be approached to locate the debtor or guarantor, the bank's own staff do it without causing nuisance (46.7).

playbook.why: The core is an HKMA 'must not', never traded: agencies must not use intimidation or violence, and banks and their agencies must not try to recover from anyone who has not guaranteed the debt (HKMA Guideline 3.4.1; see also CoBP 46.2–46.3). The rest comes from the Code of Banking Practice, which a digital bank should observe (Digital Bank Guideline para 21), and the statutory processor terms sit in the data processor clause (PDPO DPP2(3), DPP4(2)).
preferred: **Conduct rules as obligations:** the CoBP 46.1–46.3 rules written into the agreement as duties of the agency and every collector, with the bank's written instructions able to add to them (CoBP 46.4; HKMA Guideline 3.4.1).
**Principal and agent, no sub-contracting:** the agreement states the relationship is principal and agent and bars any sub-contracting of collection (CoBP 46.5). See the sub-contracting clause.

**Bank keeps control:** no legal proceedings without the bank's formal approval, only bank-approved recovery methods, no charges beyond what the bank specifies, and an immediate stop once the agency learns of full settlement or a bankruptcy order (CoBP 46.11, 46.13, 47.3–47.4, 47.9).

**Visibility and remedies:** recorded calls and contact logs kept for [6] months, unscheduled inspection visits, complaints referred to the bank promptly, cooperation and remediation, and termination for unacceptable practices or any breach (CoBP 47.5–47.8, 47.12).
fallback: **Recording period:** accept the Code minimum of 30 days for recordings and contact records instead of the bank's longer period, only if records about any complaint or dispute are kept until it is resolved (CoBP 47.5, 47.7).
**Field contacts:** if an agency cannot record face-to-face contacts, accept detailed contact reports for them, only if all telephone calls are recorded and debtors are told why (CoBP 47.5).

**Standard agency form:** accept the agency's paper with the bank's conduct rules incorporated as binding written instructions, only if breach is a breach of contract and a termination ground, and the paper itself states principal and agent, bars sub-contracting and data sharing, and withholds authority to sue (CoBP 46.3–46.5, 47.9, 47.11–47.12).

**Liability cap:** accept a cap on the agency's liability, only if it does not limit liability for breach of the conduct rules, confidentiality or data protection. See the liability and insurance clause.
redLines: **Conduct floor:** no intimidation or violence, no harassment or improper tactics, and no recovery from referees, family or friends who have not guaranteed the debt, binding on every collector (CoBP 46.1–46.4; HKMA Guideline 3.4.1).
**Agency structure:** principal and agent stated, no sub-contracting of collection, and no authority to sue without the bank's formal approval (CoBP 46.5, 47.9).

**Customer data:** data privacy clauses barring sharing of customer information with anyone else, including other agencies (CoBP 47.11), plus the processor terms the bank uses to meet its own PDPO duty (PDPO DPP2(3), DPP4(2)). See the data processor clause.
model: (a) The Supplier acts as the Bank's agent in collecting the debts the Bank refers to it, and the relationship between them is that of principal and agent. The Supplier shall not sub-contract or delegate the collection of any debt to any other person, and shall not commence legal proceedings against any debtor without the Bank's prior formal written approval.

(b) The Supplier shall ensure that every person collecting debts for it acts within Applicable Law, does nothing prejudicial to the Bank's business, integrity, reputation or goodwill, keeps all Customer Data strictly confidential, and complies with the conduct rules in [Schedule [ ] (Collection Conduct Rules)] and any further written instructions the Bank issues, which form part of this Agreement.

(c) Without limiting paragraph (b), no person collecting for the Supplier shall: use or threaten intimidation or violence; act to humiliate a debtor publicly; make persistent calls or messages, or calls at unreasonable hours; contact a debtor's referees, or pester the debtor's family or friends; use a false name or anonymous communications; make abusive, threatening, false or misleading statements; or seek payment from anyone who has not formally guaranteed the debt.

(d) Each collector shall identify themselves and the Bank and, on request, show the Bank's letter of authority, which contains no account details. The Supplier shall use only recovery methods the Bank approves, demand no more than the Bank specifies, take payment only into accounts the Bank designates, and stop all recovery at once, telling the Bank, on learning that a debt is settled in full or a bankruptcy order has been made.

(e) The Supplier shall tell each debtor that telephone calls are recorded and why, record all telephone calls, and keep a record of every other contact showing the collector, the date, time and place, and a report of the contact. It shall retain those recordings and records for [6] months after the contact, and in any event for at least 30 days, and until any related complaint is resolved.

(f) The Bank may inspect the Supplier's premises, records and activities without notice. The Supplier shall refer any complaint it receives to the Bank [within [1] Business Day], cooperate in investigations and take the remedial action the Bank requires. It shall not share Customer Data with anyone else, including another agency, unless Applicable Law requires, and shall comply with [the data processor clause]. The Bank may terminate at once for any breach of this clause.
watchFor: **Free hand on methods:** a clause leaving recovery methods or contact frequency to the agency's 'industry-standard practice'; the Code says agencies should not be given a free hand (CoBP 47.3).
**Sub-agents by another name:** references to affiliates, field agents or partners making visits or calls; that is the sub-contracting the contract should bar (CoBP 46.5).

**Responsibility pushed onto the bank:** wording that has the bank disclaim responsibility to customers for the agency, or caps the agency's liability for conduct breaches at its fees; the bank stays accountable to customers either way (CoBP 46.5).
**Data reuse:** a right to use debtor data for other clients, analytics or tracing databases (CoBP 47.11). See the data processor clause.

pushback.says: We need to contact referees and family to trace debtors.
pushback.reply: This is a must-have. HKMA Guideline 3.4.1 says banks and their agencies must not try to recover a debt from anyone who has not formally guaranteed it, and asks banks to tell agencies so in writing (see also CoBP 46.3). If a referee must be approached to locate a debtor, our own staff will do it (CoBP 46.7).

pushback.says: Everyone in the industry uses trusted sub-agents for field work.
pushback.reply: The Code says our contract should bar sub-contracting collection (CoBP 46.5). If you need field capacity, use your own staff, who are covered by our conduct rules and inspection rights.

pushback.says: Thirty days is the Code minimum for recordings; keeping them longer costs more.
pushback.reply: Thirty days is the floor (CoBP 47.5). We need records kept while a complaint is open so we can investigate it properly (47.7); beyond that, the period is a cost discussion.

playbook.escalate: Suggest the Head of Collections and Head of Legal sign off deviations, with Compliance approving any departure from the Code's conduct rules; a refused red line should mean the agency is not appointed.

terms.title: Marketing and distribution partners
terms.summary: Partners who promote the bank's products, run its digital channels or sell third-party products through it expose the bank to Code and PDPO duties that the contract has to carry.
require: **Fair promotion:** the bank is responsible for ensuring that the promotional activities and materials its engaged or collaborating partners publish or share during the engagement are fair and reasonable, not misleading, and compliant with CoBP 11.2, 11.4 and 11.6 (11.7). Approval, take-down and control rights over partner materials, and over any sub-affiliates or publishers the partner uses, follow from this (drafting inference). The bank should also keep a convenient channel for the public to verify promotions by third parties it engages (11.8).
**Records:** proper records of digital marketing materials and communications kept for a reasonable period, and not left to the channel provider unless the contract provides for it (11.5).

**Agents' conduct:** authorized agents should have as an objective to work in customers' best interests and endeavour to avoid conflicts; where a conflict cannot be avoided they should disclose it, manage it or decline the business; and, where appropriate, their remuneration should encourage responsible conduct and fair treatment and avoid conflicts (2.5, a general principle).

**Third-party products:** the bank's own duties on terms and conditions (making them available, answering queries, advising customers to read them and allowing time to review: 5.1, 5.8) apply to third-party products too; the provider is told of the rest of section 5 and asked to observe it as far as possible (5.15). The agreement clearly defines each party's responsibilities for handling disputes, and lets the bank obtain the information it needs to help customers in dispute resolution (11.14).

sources.label: PDPO (Cap. 486)
sources.note: Using customers' data in direct marketing needs prescribed notice and consent (ss.35C, 35E); providing it to another person for that person's direct marketing needs written notice and written consent (ss.35J–35K). On first use the data user must tell the person of the right to opt out, and must comply with any opt-out (ss.35F–35G); a person given data for its own direct marketing must stop using it once notified in writing of an opt-out (s.35L(5)). The provision rules do not apply to data given to an agent marketing on the data user's behalf (s.35I(2)).

drafting: **Data flows:** decide whether the partner processes data only for the bank (a data processor: the bank needs contractual or other means under DPP2(3) and DPP4(2), and if the partner markets to the bank's customers, that is the bank's own use in direct marketing and needs notice and consent under PDPO ss.35C and 35E) or for its own marketing (a provision of data needing written notice and written consent under ss.35J–35K). Name partners such as co-branding or loyalty-programme providers specifically in customer notices (CoBP 8.3), and draft accordingly.

playbook.why: The core comes from the Code of Banking Practice, which is non-statutory but monitored by the HKMA (CoBP 1.4), and which the Digital Bank Guideline says a digital bank should observe (para 21). Where a partner uses Customer Data for direct marketing, PDPO Part 6A is statute backed by criminal offences, and that part is the floor.
preferred: **Bank approval of materials and publishers:** every promotional material or activity naming the bank or its products, and every sub-affiliate, publisher or influencer used, approved by the bank in advance, with amendment and take-down on notice; the bank is responsible for partners' materials during the engagement (CoBP 11.2, 11.4, 11.6–11.7).

**Records and verification:** the partner keeps, and delivers on request, all materials and related customer communications for [2] years, and supports the bank's channel for the public to check that promotions are genuine (CoBP 11.5, 11.8).

**Direct marketing only within the bank's consents:** Customer Data collected under bank-approved notices and consent wording, used for direct marketing only on the bank's behalf within the consents it holds, with first-use opt-out notices given and opt-outs acted on at once, and never for the partner's own marketing (PDPO ss.35C, 35E–35G, 35J–35K).

**Agent conduct and disputes:** authorized agents work in customers' best interests, avoid or disclose and manage conflicts, and are not paid in ways that reward unfair selling; dispute-handling roles and information flows are set out (CoBP 2.5, 11.14).
fallback: **Template approval:** accept bank-approved templates and messaging rules with spot checks instead of approving each item, only if new products, rate or fee claims and offer conditions still need prior approval and take-down stays immediate (CoBP 11.2, 11.6–11.7).
**Channel-held records:** accept that the channel provider keeps the records, only if the contract binds it to the agreed period and to prompt delivery on request (CoBP 11.5).

**Third-party product providers:** where the provider's own contract governs the product, accept its undertaking to follow the Code's terms-and-conditions practices as far as possible, only if it gives the bank what it needs to answer queries and assist in disputes (CoBP 5.15, 11.14).

**Partner's own customers:** where the partner is a data user for its own members, as in a co-branded programme, accept that status, only if any Customer Data given to it for its own marketing has the bank's written notice and the customer's written consent, and the bank's notices name the partner (PDPO ss.35J–35L; CoBP 8.3(d)).
redLines: **Control of promotions:** no engagement without the bank's control over content and over who publishes it, and an immediate take-down right; the bank is responsible for its partners' promotional materials (CoBP 11.7).

**PDPO direct marketing and processing:** no use or provision of Customer Data for direct marketing outside the bank's notices and consents, first-use notices given and opt-outs honoured (PDPO ss.35C, 35E–35G, 35J–35L); if the partner processes Customer Data for the bank, contractual or other means, usually the data processor clause terms (PDPO DPP2(3), DPP4(2)).
model: (a) Without the Bank's prior written approval, the Supplier shall not engage any sub-affiliate, publisher or influencer to promote the Bank, or publish, share or carry out, or let any of them do so, any material or activity promoting the Bank or its products or services. All such material shall be fair and reasonable, not misleading, state clearly any conditions of a promotional benefit, and comply with Applicable Law and [Schedule [ ] (Marketing Guidelines)].

(b) On the Bank's notice, the Supplier shall amend, suspend or withdraw any such material or activity [within [4] hours], including where a benefit is no longer available. It shall keep copies of all such material, campaign records and related customer communications for [at least [2] years] after each campaign, deliver them [within [2] Business Days] of request, and support any channel the Bank provides for the public to verify its promotions.

(c) The Supplier shall use Personal Data it receives or collects for the Bank only on the Bank's behalf, within the purposes, kinds of data, marketing subjects and consents the Bank specifies in writing, and never for its own marketing or for provision to anyone else. It shall collect such data only under notices and consent wording the Bank approves, and keep records of each consent for the Bank.

(d) The Supplier shall include in its first direct marketing communication to each person the opt-out notice the Bank specifies. It shall stop using a person's data in direct marketing immediately on receiving that person's opt-out or the Bank's notice of one, and shall pass any opt-out it receives to the Bank [within [1] Business Day].

(e) Where the Supplier deals with customers as the Bank's authorized agent, it shall work in their best interests, avoid conflicts of interest and, where a conflict cannot be avoided, disclose and manage it or decline the business, and shall not remunerate its staff in a way that rewards sales at the expense of fair treatment of customers.

(f) Where the Bank distributes the Supplier's products, the Supplier shall give the Bank the product terms for customers, answer queries the Bank refers to it, observe so far as possible the terms-and-conditions practices in section 5 of the Code of Banking Practice, and give the Bank [within [5] Business Days] of request the information and documents it needs to assist a customer in a dispute, as allocated in [Schedule [ ] (Dispute Handling)].
watchFor: **Creative freedom and sub-publishers:** partner editorial control, deemed approval if the bank does not respond within a short time, or a free hand to use sub-affiliates, publishers or influencers; the bank stays responsible for what engaged parties publish and should give the public a way to verify them (CoBP 11.7–11.8).

**Data rights for the partner:** a licence to use customer or campaign data for its own marketing, audience-building or 'service improvement'; that can be a provision for direct marketing needing written consent (PDPO ss.35J–35K). See the data processor clause.
**Short platform retention:** standard terms that delete posts, messages or campaign records on a short cycle, leaving the bank unable to deal with enquiries and complaints (CoBP 11.5).
**Volume-only commission:** pay tied only to sign-ups or sales, with no quality or complaint adjustment; remuneration should encourage fair treatment and avoid conflicts (CoBP 2.5).

pushback.says: Approving every post will kill engagement; we know our audience.
pushback.reply: The Code makes the bank responsible for your promotional materials during the engagement (CoBP 11.7). We can pre-approve templates and turn new content round quickly, but we keep approval and take-down rights.

pushback.says: Data collected through the campaign is ours to use.
pushback.reply: Customer Data you receive or collect for us is used only for us. Giving it to you for your own direct marketing would need written notice and written consent we have not obtained, and doing it without them would be an offence by us (PDPO ss.35J–35K); your own use would also need your own notice and consent (ss.35C, 35E). For a co-branded programme, we can discuss a consent-based route.

pushback.says: Our platform keeps records for 90 days as standard.
pushback.reply: We must keep proper records for a reasonable period and cannot leave it to a channel provider without contract terms (CoBP 11.5). Commit to the agreed period or give us a full export so we keep them.

playbook.escalate: Suggest the Head of Marketing and Head of Legal approve deviations, with the Data Protection Officer signing off any change to data use and Compliance any departure from the Code-based terms.

intro: **How to use it:** for each clause in the vendor's draft, check the red lines first. Then mark up towards the preferred position using the model wording, and use the watch-for list to spot drafting that needs a markup. Fallbacks are compromises already cleared for use, but only on their stated conditions; pushback gives short answers to common objections. The tags on each clause show which contracts it applies to.

**Three stances:** must-have means the core comes from statute, from a statutory guideline, or from something an HKMA source says the MA must be satisfied of or the bank must do. Do not sign without it. Expected means the core comes from non-statutory HKMA guidance (SA-2, TM-G-1, OR-2) or the Code of Banking Practice. Negotiable means good practice only, traded commercially; no clause in this kit is negotiable overall. Where only part of a clause is mandatory, its red lines mark that floor.

**Handling a deviation:** every fallback still meets the must-have floor. Anything beyond a fallback needs a written rationale, compensating controls and sign-off at the level suggested below, recorded in the vendor risk file. If a vendor refuses a must-have, escalate and consider whether the arrangement can go ahead; for material outsourcing, consider discussing it with the HKMA (SA-2 1.3.2; Digital Bank Guideline para 23). Falling short on an expected term can bear on whether the bank still meets the Seventh Schedule criteria (SA-2 1.2.2).

**Brackets:** square brackets mark drafting choices and figures, such as [30] days or [Schedule 3]. The figures are illustrative and not from the sources. Set them from the bank's own risk assessment and tolerances for disruption. Where statute fixes the bank's own deadline, as Cap. 653 s.28 and Sch. 6 do for incident notice, the playbook states it accurately and gives the Supplier a shorter deadline in brackets.

**Status:** this is study material, written as counsel's drafting from the documents supplied. It is not legal advice and not HKMA text: the sources are paraphrased and the model wording is original. Before relying on it, check the current versions (CG-1 was checked against V.4, 1 August 2025; later HKMA circulars were not supplied, so check) and take advice.

definitions.meaning: the authorized institution that is a party to this Agreement.
the party that provides the Services under this Agreement.
the services described in this Agreement and its schedules, including any deliverables and anything incidental to them [or reasonably necessary for their proper performance].

the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), including the Monetary Authority acting under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155), and any other authority, in or outside Hong Kong, with supervisory, regulatory or resolution powers over the Bank or any member of its group. It includes anyone acting for or appointed by any of them, such as an Advisor or Manager appointed under section 52 of the Banking Ordinance, and any auditor or expert a Regulator appoints or requires the Bank to appoint.

all laws, regulations and binding orders that apply to the Bank, the Supplier or the Services, and every guideline, code, circular and requirement of a Regulator that applies to the Bank[, and any industry code the Bank observes, such as the Code of Banking Practice].

all data and information, in any form, of or about the Bank, its group or its customers that the Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, creates or holds in connection with the Services, including copies, backups, logs and metadata. It includes Customer Data.

Bank Data relating to any current, former or prospective customer of the Bank, whether an individual or a corporation, or to a guarantor, authorised signatory or other person connected with one, including Personal Data.
