deepDive.heading: Custody and wallets
deepDive.lede: Holding customers' virtual assets is a distinct risk, because control of a private key is control of the asset. Two questions matter: what the law says the asset is, and how the bank controls access to it.

visual.caption: Two questions matter: what the law says the asset is, and how the bank controls access to it.

centre.label: Who controls the private key?
centre.note: Control of the key is control of the asset

items.label: Hosted wallet
items.note: The bank is a custodian: custody guidance, segregation and its own insolvency position apply

items.label: Unhosted wallet
items.note: Withdrawals raise travel-rule and ownership checks; a typical scam route

points: **Property status:** Re Gatecoin Ltd (in liquidation) [2023] HKCFI 914 held that cryptocurrency is property capable of being held on trust. Under the 2018 terms there was no trust (disclaimers, pooling, coins treated as the company's own). Customers who never accepted them had a trust under earlier express terms.

**Documentation:** The Gatecoin outcome turned on contract wording, pooling and accounting. A bank should state client-asset status expressly, give itself no free right to use customer assets, and keep ledger and wallet segregation distinct from its own.

**HKMA guidance:** The HKMA's custody guidance for AIs, first issued on 20 February 2024 and updated on 27 May 2026, covers governance, segregation, private-key handling, outsourcing, disclosure, reconciliation and AML. Read the current annex in full.

**Hosted wallets:** In a hosted (custodial) wallet the bank or its sub-custodian controls the private key. That makes the bank a custodian, so the custody guidance, client-asset segregation and its own insolvency position all apply.

**Unhosted wallets:** In an [[unhosted wallet]] the customer controls the key. Withdrawals to such wallets raise travel-rule and ownership-verification questions and are a typical scam route, so they need specific controls.

**Proposed regime:** Dealing and custody licensing under AMLO is still a bill proposal. A custodian licence is expected to turn on safekeeping private keys or similar means of transfer; whether banks are exempted or deemed is not confirmed.
deepDive.takeaway: Custody is where legal form, technology and operations meet. Draft the customer terms and the key-management design together, and test both against a bank-insolvency scenario.

deepDive.heading: Stablecoins under Cap. 656 and the bank's possible roles
deepDive.lede: The Stablecoins Ordinance has applied since 1 August 2025. Only issuance needs a licence today, but a bank can touch the regime as issuer, offeror, reserve bank, custodian or payment acceptor.

visual.caption: Only issuance needs a licence today; offering is restricted under s.9. Be clear who the issuer, offeror and custodian are.

items.label: Issuer
items.note: Needs a Cap. 656 licence; a banking licence is not one

items.label: Offeror
items.note: To retail, licensed issuers' coins only (inference)

items.label: Reserve bank or custodian
items.note: Reserve deposits are outside the DPS

items.label: Ads for unlicensed activity
items.note: Knowing publication is an offence

points: **Definition:** Under s.3 a stablecoin is a DLT-based digital value that aims to hold stable value against one or more assets. A [[specified stablecoin]] is one referenced wholly to official currencies, or to other units or stores of value the MA specifies (s.4). Deposits, SVF float and securities are excluded.

**Issuing:** s.8 makes it an offence to carry on a regulated stablecoin activity without a licence, and a banking licence is not one. An AI may apply under s.14. The HKMA issued its first two licences on 10 April 2026.

**Offering:** s.9 restricts offering a specified stablecoin. An AI is a permitted offeror under s.9(5), but the coin must also be licence-issued, or the offeree must be in a specified class. L.N. 126 of 2025, made under s.9(3), specifies professional investors.
**Retail effect:** In practice a bank can offer retail customers only coins of licensed issuers. The Ordinance does not use the word retail, so this is an inference from s.9(2) and the notice.

**Reserve banking:** Sch. 2 s.5 lets issuers hold the reserve pool directly or by arrangement, which is the hook for banks acting as account bank or reserve custodian. Reserve deposits are excluded from the DPS under Cap. 581 Sch. 1 s.1(j).

**Marketing and fraud:** s.10 criminalises knowingly publishing advertisements for unlicensed activity, and ss.11 and 12 create fraud and misrepresentation offences. Expect scams that misuse licensed issuers' names.
**Licensing pace:** LCQ6 of 10 June 2026 said the HKMA had received 36 applications and licensed two. Future licences will be very limited.
deepDive.takeaway: Treat licensed stablecoins as a separate product line with its own gates: HKMA discussion, any current HKMA circular on stablecoin activities by registered institutions, and a clear answer on who the issuer, offeror and custodian are.

deepDive.heading: Tokenised deposits, tokenised securities, Project Ensemble and e-HKD
deepDive.lede: Tokenisation changes the record-keeping, not the legal character. The bank should ask what claim the token represents, then apply the regime for that claim.

visual.caption: Tokenisation changes the record-keeping, not the legal character.

centre.label: A tokenised product
centre.note: What claim does the token represent?

items.label: Tokenised deposit
items.note: Stays a bank liability; outside the stablecoin definition

items.label: Tokenised security
items.note: Due diligence on issuer, vendors and arrangement

items.label: Same product, new wrapper
items.note: Added controls for due diligence, disclosure and custody

items.label: Project Ensemble; e-HKD
items.note: Pilots, not law; no retail e-HKD decision found

points: **Tokenised deposits:** A [[tokenised deposit]] that is a deposit under Cap. 155 s.2(1) is excluded from the stablecoin definition by Cap. 656 s.3(2)(e). It stays a bank liability, so check that no design feature, such as a bearer-style token, falls into a DPS exclusion.

**Tokenised products:** The HKMA's circular of 20 February 2024 treats non-SFO tokenised products as the same product in a new wrapper, with added controls for due diligence, disclosure and custody. Whether it extends to tokenised deposits is not confirmed, so read the text.

**Tokenised securities:** SFC circular 23EC52 of 2 November 2023 expects intermediaries to do due diligence on the issuer, vendors and tokenisation arrangement. On 20 April 2026 the SFC replaced its 2 November 2023 circular on tokenising SFC-authorised products and issued one on secondary trading on licensed VATPs. 23EC52 still applies.

**Project Ensemble:** Launched in March 2024, with a sandbox from August 2024 and the EnsembleTX pilot announced in November 2025 for real-value tokenised deposit transactions. [[Project Ensemble]] is a pilot, not law, and participation terms are contractual.
**e-HKD:** The HKMA has run e-HKD pilots and has given more priority to wholesale tokenised money. No decision to launch a retail [[e-HKD]] was found. Do not plan a product that depends on it.
**Government bonds:** The HKMA's digital green bond issues show the tokenised settlement use case. They are issuance announcements, not rules for banks.
deepDive.takeaway: Treat tokenised deposits as a deposit product with new operational risk, and pilots as commercial opportunities that require HKMA and legal sign-off at contract level.

deepDive.heading: Capital and risk management for crypto exposures
deepDive.lede: Holding crypto-assets or taking them as collateral is expensive in capital terms. Hong Kong implemented the Basel cryptoasset standard from 1 January 2026.
points: **Basel groups:** SCO60 sorts cryptoassets into Group 1a (tokenised traditional assets), Group 1b (stabilised assets) and Group 2 (the rest). Group 2 is split into 2a and 2b, and the Group 2b treatment is a 1250% risk weight.

**Group 2 limit:** Under the Basel standard, Group 2 exposure should stay below 1% of Tier 1 capital and must not exceed 2%. In Hong Kong, Capital Rules s.388 applies the limit only to G-SIBs and D-SIBs, so a digital bank should set its own internal cap.

**Local rules:** The Banking (Capital), (Disclosure) and (Exposure Limits) (Amendment) Rules 2025 were gazetted on 11 July 2025 and took effect on 1 January 2026, made under Cap. 155 ss.97C, 60A and 81A respectively. The HKMA's SPM module CRP-1 (Classification of Cryptoassets, V.1, effective 1 January 2026) sets classification conditions.

**Classification:** CRP-1 includes measures that can let permissionless-blockchain assets qualify. An HKMA letter of 3 June 2026 clarified para 2.6.4 of CRP-1; check for later clarifications. Classification should be documented per asset, not per platform.

**Disclosure and review:** Crypto disclosure templates and the revised CA-D-1 apply from 1 January 2026. The Basel Committee agreed in November 2025 to expedite a targeted review, with an update promised later in 2026. No revised standard was found as at 27 October 2026.

**Lending against crypto:** No HKMA rule specific to bank lending against crypto collateral was found. Treat any SFC guidance on VA margin financing as a market reference, not a bank rule, and use CRP-1 and custody guidance.
deepDive.takeaway: For a digital bank with thin capital headroom, the capital cost of Group 2 crypto will often decide the business case before the legal route does.

deepDive.heading: Financial crime: VASP customers, VA transfers and scams
deepDive.lede: Digital assets reach the bank through customers, counterparties and payment flows. The AML framework in the earlier AML and fraud stage still applies; this section adds the VA-specific points.

visual.caption: These need data fields and tooling in the payments stack.

items.label: Travel rule
items.note: Originator and recipient information; fewer originator details below HK$8,000

items.label: VASP customers
items.note: Risk-based onboarding, not blanket de-risking

items.label: Stablecoin issuers
items.note: Reserve accounts still need the bank's own CDD

items.label: Other banks
items.note: ML and TF information on designated platforms

points: **VASP customers:** An HKMA circular of 27 April 2023 asked banks to support SFC-licensed VASPs' legitimate need for accounts using a risk-based approach. Banking a VASP outside Hong Kong may engage the correspondent-type measures in the HKMA Guideline paras 11.23 to 11.25.

**Travel rule:** AMLO Sch. 2 s.13A requires an institution sending a [[VA transfer|travel rule]] to obtain, record and send originator and recipient information. Below HK$8,000 the originator's address, ID number or birth details need not be collected. Recipient and intermediary institutions have separate duties.

**CDD trigger:** HKMA AML/CFT Guideline para 4.2.1(b)(iii) requires CDD for occasional VA transfers of HK$8,000 or more, with footnote 15 pointing to s.13A. A customer with an existing relationship is not an occasional case.

**Counterparty risk:** Where the bank is a registered institution, HKMA Guideline footnote 1 points to the SFC AML guideline, including its virtual asset chapter. Check the current chapter text for self-hosted wallet expectations.

**Scams and mules:** The FPS Suspicious Proxy ID Alert, launched in November 2023, has been extended to other channels. Since 3 November 2025, Cap. 155 Part XIIAA lets banks share ML and TF information on designated platforms. Crypto cash-outs and fake-token scams belong in the same typologies.

**Stablecoin issuers:** A licensed issuer is an AMLO financial institution, and the HKMA's AML guideline for issuers expects travel-rule compliance and requires issuers to ascertain ownership or control of every customer wallet. Reserve account relationships still need the bank's own CDD.
deepDive.takeaway: The travel rule, wallet screening and VASP due diligence need data fields and tooling in the payments stack, so involve engineering before the product is approved.

deepDive.heading: P2P and platform lending
deepDive.lede: Banks fund and partner with platforms more often than they run them. The law differs sharply depending on who makes the loan and who holds the investor's money.

visual.caption: Decide first whether the bank is lender, funder or merely a bank account provider.

centre.label: Your bank and a lending platform

items.label: The bank's own loan
items.note: CoBP and the HKMA BNPL and cooling-off circulars apply
items.rel: if the bank lends through it

items.label: Licensed money lender
items.note: Licence, 48% rate cap; check the register

items.label: Possible CIS or securities
items.note: SFC warning on pooled structures

items.label: Arranging fees
items.note: Restricted; review fee flows before launch
items.rel: if borrowers are charged for arranging

points: **Bank exemption:** The Money Lenders Ordinance does not apply to an AI (s.3), and a subsidiary of an AI is an exempted person under Sch. 1 Pt 1 para 1. The bank's own lending is governed by the Banking Ordinance, the HKMA and the Code of Banking Practice.

**Non-bank lenders:** A non-bank [[money lender]] needs a licence (s.7), faces a 48% rate cap (s.24) and a 36% extortionate presumption (s.25), and has advertising rules under s.26. Check the Registrar's public register before funding or partnering.

**P2P structures:** [[P2P lending]] has no dedicated Hong Kong regime. The SFC has warned that pooled or participation structures may be collective investment schemes or securities, and lenders on a platform may need a money lender licence.

**Bank-originated loans:** Where the bank lends through a platform or buy-now-pay-later partner, the loan is the bank's. the HKMA's September 2022 circular on buy-now-pay-later, the Code of Banking Practice and the November 2024 cooling-off circular for unsecured consumer credit apply.

**Referral fees:** MLO s.27 restricts charging borrowers for arranging a loan, and licence conditions regulate third-party introducers. Fee flows between a platform, a lender and the bank need review before launch.

**Debt collection:** The bank stays responsible for collection by agencies under the Code of Banking Practice, and licensed lenders have their own conduct conditions. See Customers & conduct and Technology & outsourcing for the wider framework.
deepDive.takeaway: Decide first whether the bank is lender, funder or merely a bank account provider, then check each counterparty's status and the SFO angle if investors pool money.

deepDive.heading: Web3: staking, DeFi, NFTs, DAOs and smart contracts
deepDive.lede: Web3 features are often marketing-led and arrive through partners. Most have no dedicated Hong Kong rule, so the existing perimeter does the work.
points: **Staking:** The HKMA and SFC issued parallel circulars on 7 April 2025 allowing staking in defined conditions, and the joint circular supplement of 30 September 2025 also allows staking on conditions. An AI offering staking from custody should discuss it with the HKMA first and keep control of withdrawal mechanics.

**[[DeFi]]:** No dedicated SFC or HKMA circular was found. The SFC has said DeFi activity within SFO scope is regulated like traditional activity, and its ASPIRe roadmap of 19 February 2025 flags smart contract and scam risk. Treat bank access to DeFi as a high-risk exception.

**NFTs and tokens:** The SFC's 6 June 2022 statement treats unique collectibles as generally outside its remit, but fractionalised or fungible interests may be securities or CIS. A loyalty token fails the limited purpose test if it is tradeable or convertible to cash.

**DAOs:** A governance token can be a VA, since s.53ZRA(1)(a)(ii)(B) expressly covers tokens giving governance voting rights, unless it is a security or otherwise excluded. Interacting with a DAO also raises legal-personality and liability questions.

**[[Smart contracts|smart contract]]:** The Electronic Transactions Ordinance supports electronic offer, acceptance and signatures, but does not itself validate code as contract. No Hong Kong court decision or law reform report on smart contract enforceability was found.

**Names and advertising:** Cap. 155 s.97 restricts use of bank names, s.92 restricts deposit invitations by anyone other than an AI, and AMLO s.53ZRE and Cap. 656 s.10 restrict advertisements for unlicensed services. Apply these to app screens, partner pages and metaverse content.
deepDive.takeaway: For Web3 ideas, map each feature to an existing perimeter rule, document that analysis, and avoid representations that a token is a deposit, a stablecoin or guaranteed.

deepDive.heading: What is coming next
deepDive.lede: Several items are proposals or pilots. Track them, but do not build contracts or customer promises that assume they will pass.
points: **Dealing and custody:** The consultation conclusions of 24 December 2025 on VA dealing and custody licensing propose new AMLO regimes. No bill had been introduced as at late September 2026, so check the legislative timetable.

**Advisory and management:** Consultation conclusions of 26 May 2026 propose regimes modelled on Types 4 and 9 under the AMLO, to be legislated with dealing and custody. No bill as at late September 2026. Whether banks get a distinct route is unconfirmed.
**Stablecoins:** The HKMA may add regulated activities to Cap. 656 by notice under s.5(4). No such notice was found. A third issuer licence has not been found either.

**Tokenisation:** Policy Statement 2.0 (26 June 2025) promises a legal review of tokenised bond settlement and record-keeping. Testing of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills is reported for 2026, but not confirmed.

**Capital and lending:** The Basel Committee's targeted cryptoasset review is pending, with an update promised later in 2026, and money lender licensing conditions continue to be revised. The Banking Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2026 is still under scrutiny.
deepDive.takeaway: Build a watch list with owners and dates, and recheck the position before each product committee.

provisions.instrument: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
provisions.title: Meaning of virtual asset
provisions.summary: Defines a virtual asset as a cryptographically secured digital representation of value used or intended as a medium of exchange accepted by the public, or conferring governance voting rights, and transferable or tradable electronically. It excludes central bank money, limited purpose tokens, securities and futures contracts, and SVF float.
provisions.counselNote: Use this as the first filter in the triage. A token that is a security or SVF balance is not a VA, and a governance token may be. Confirm whether the SFC has prescribed further characteristics.

provisions.instrument: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
provisions.title: Licence required for VA service business
provisions.summary: Prohibits carrying on, or holding out as carrying on, a VA service business without an SFC licence. The only VA service defined today is operating a VA exchange where client money or client VAs come into the operator's possession. Penalties on indictment reach HK$5,000,000 and 7 years.
provisions.counselNote: Part 5B has no general AI exemption, so on counsel's reading a bank operating an exchange would need a licence. That is an inference, not an SFC statement; a bank routing orders to a licensed VATP is unlikely to be operating the exchange itself.

provisions.instrument: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
provisions.title: Advertisements for unlicensed VA services
provisions.summary: Makes it an offence knowingly to issue an advertisement, including by social media or electronic means, for a person who is not licensed for a VA service. There are due diligence and conduit defences, and an advertisement issued on behalf of another is treated as issued by both.
provisions.counselNote: Relevant to app banners, partner promotions and affiliate content. Build a pre-publication check of the partner's licence status against the SFC register.

provisions.instrument: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
provisions.title: Travel rule for virtual asset transfers
provisions.summary: Requires ordering institutions to obtain, record and send originator and recipient information with a VA transfer, and sets duties for beneficiary and intermediary institutions. Below HK$8,000 the originator's address, identification number or date and place of birth need not be obtained or sent, but the name is still required. A beneficiary or intermediary institution that cannot obtain missing data must consider restricting the relationship with the instructing institution or take reasonable mitigating measures.
provisions.counselNote: Needs a pricing and linked-transaction rule for the HK$8,000 test and a messaging solution for counterparties. Define what happens to inbound transfers that arrive without data.

provisions.title: Registered institutions
provisions.summary: Allows an authorized financial institution to apply to the SFC to be registered for regulated activities other than Types 3 and 8. The SFC refers the application to the MA, who advises on fitness and properness, and may impose conditions on registration.
provisions.counselNote: This is the gateway for VA dealing, advice, management and distribution. The SFC can impose and amend registration conditions under s.119(5), so check what VA-related conditions attach to the bank's registration. Which types apply depends on the activity; confirm with the SFC and HKMA.

provisions.instrument: HKMA and SFC joint circular on intermediaries' virtual asset-related activities
provisions.title: Joint circular on VA-related activities
provisions.summary: Sets the framework for distribution of VA-related products, VA dealing, advisory and asset management by licensed corporations and registered institutions. It superseded the 20 October 2023 version, which had replaced the 28 January 2022 circular. The 30 September 2025 supplement allows staking on conditions and clarifies that subscriptions and redemptions in VAs are not VA dealing. Parallel circulars of 27 May 2026 cover relevant stablecoins. It expects omnibus dealing through licensed VATPs and retail investor protection.
provisions.counselNote: Paragraph numbers and the current consolidated terms were not confirmed. Obtain the latest versions of the circular and its appendices before preparing any submission.

provisions.instrument: HKMA circular, Virtual asset-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins
provisions.ref: 27 May 2026; SFC companion circular of the same date
provisions.title: Relaxations for relevant stablecoins
provisions.summary: Relaxes joint-circular requirements for registered institutions dealing, advising or managing assets in stablecoins of HKMA-licensed issuers. Reported changes include dropping the VA knowledge test for clients holding only such coins and streamlined suitability. AIs are told to discuss with the HKMA in advance.
provisions.counselNote: Relaxations apply only to relevant stablecoins and to registered institutions. A bank that is not registered should not assume they apply. Read the full text.

provisions.instrument: HKMA circular, Updated Guidance on Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets
provisions.title: HKMA custody guidance for AIs
provisions.summary: Sets expected standards for AIs holding virtual assets, tokenised securities and other tokenised assets for clients, covering governance, segregation, private keys, outsourcing, disclosure, reconciliation and AML. The 27 May 2026 update supersedes and expands the 2024 guidance and, per law-firm reports, adds a training requirement for transaction signers.
provisions.counselNote: Reports of a specific cold-storage ratio are unverified. Confirm compliance deadlines and whether stablecoin reserve custody is treated as custody for this purpose.

provisions.instrument: HKMA circular, Sale and distribution of tokenised products
provisions.title: Tokenised products circular
provisions.summary: Treats non-SFO tokenised products, such as tokenised structured investment products or spot precious metal, as the same product in a new wrapper. Existing supervisory and investor protection requirements for the underlying product apply, with additional controls for tokenisation risks.
provisions.counselNote: Keep tokenised products separate from VA-related products in governance papers.

provisions.title: Tokenised securities and authorised products
provisions.summary: 23EC52 sets expectations for intermediaries dealing in, advising on or managing tokenised securities, including due diligence on the issuer, vendors and tokenisation arrangement. On 20 April 2026 the SFC replaced its 2 November 2023 circular on tokenising SFC-authorised products and issued a circular on secondary trading of tokenised authorised products on licensed VATPs. 23EC52 still applies.
provisions.counselNote: Applies to a bank acting as a registered institution. Paragraph numbers and the treatment of bank custody were not confirmed from the SFC texts.

provisions.title: Meaning of stablecoin
provisions.summary: Defines a stablecoin as a cryptographically secured digital representation of value on a distributed ledger that aims to keep stable value against assets. It excludes central bank money, limited purpose tokens, securities, SVF float and deposits within Cap. 155 s.2(1).
provisions.counselNote: The exclusion of deposits in s.3(2)(e) is the statutory basis for treating tokenised deposits as deposits. Document the analysis for each token design.

provisions.title: Offence to carry on regulated stablecoin activity without licence
provisions.summary: Prohibits carrying on, or holding out as carrying on, a regulated stablecoin activity unless licensed or exempted. Penalties on indictment reach HK$5,000,000 and 7 years. Regulated activity means issuing a specified stablecoin in Hong Kong, or elsewhere if it references Hong Kong dollars, with a power in s.5(4) to add more.
provisions.counselNote: A banking licence does not cover issuance. Any plan for a group or partner to issue a coin needs a licence analysis and an HKMA conversation early.

provisions.title: Offering a specified stablecoin
provisions.summary: Makes it an offence to offer a specified stablecoin unless an exception applies. The main exception is a permitted offeror where the issue is licence-authorized. An authorized institution is a permitted offeror under s.9(5).
provisions.counselNote: Being a permitted offeror is not enough by itself. Confirm that the coin is licence-issued, or that the offeree falls within a specified class, before it appears in the app.

provisions.instrument: Payment Systems and Stored Value Facilities Ordinance (Cap. 584)
provisions.title: Bank regarded as SVF licensee
provisions.summary: Regards a bank as granted an SVF licence under s.8F when it is granted a banking licence. Several licensee-only provisions, including the licence fee and certain intervention divisions, do not apply to a bank, while safe-operation duties still do.
provisions.counselNote: A wallet feature can sit on the bank's deemed SVF licence, but a balance held in stablecoins or VAs needs separate analysis under Cap. 656 and AMLO. Check the single-purpose and exempt categories before treating a balance as unregulated.

provisions.title: Deposits excluded from DPS protection
provisions.summary: Lists exclusions from protected deposits, including bearer instruments, structured deposits, SVF float and deposits comprising stablecoin reserve assets. No exclusion for tokenised form was found.
provisions.counselNote: No DPS Board or HKMA statement on tokenised deposits was found. Confirm that the token design does not fall into an exclusion and that customer disclosure is consistent.

provisions.instrument: Basel Framework SCO60; HKMA SPM CRP-1; Banking (Capital) Rules (Cap. 155L) Part 12 and Banking (Exposure Limits) Rules (Cap. 155S) as amended
provisions.title: Prudential treatment of cryptoasset exposures
provisions.summary: The Basel standard sorts cryptoassets into Groups 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b, with a 1250% risk weight for Group 2b and a Group 2 exposure limit. Hong Kong's implementing rules, including a Group 2 cryptoasset exposure ratio in Cap. 155L ss.387 and 388, were gazetted on 11 July 2025 (L.N. 150 to 152) and took effect on 1 January 2026. CRP-1 (V.1, effective 1 January 2026) sets classification conditions.
provisions.counselNote: Banking Ordinance s.97C is the enabling power for capital rules. Confirm the Hong Kong wording of the Group 2 limit and read CRP-1 conditions before any proprietary exposure.

provisions.instrument: HKMA circular, Risk management considerations related to the use of DLT
provisions.title: DLT risk management considerations
provisions.summary: Sets out considerations the HKMA applies in reviewing AIs' DLT proposals across governance, design and development, and ongoing maintenance and monitoring. Board and senior management are expected to take responsibility for DLT adoption.
provisions.counselNote: Use it as a checklist for any bank process that runs on a ledger or smart contract. The considerations are non-binding but are what the HKMA will ask.

provisions.instrument: HKMA Guideline on AML/CFT for Authorized Institutions (May 2023)
provisions.title: AML expectations for VA transfers and VASPs
provisions.summary: Restates the statutory duty to carry out CDD before an occasional VA transfer of HK$8,000 or more, points to Sch. 2 s.13A, and expects correspondent-type measures for services to VASPs outside Hong Kong. Registered institutions are pointed to the SFC AML guideline.
provisions.counselNote: Separate own-account and customer-facing VASP activity where possible, as paras 11.24 and 11.25 suggest. The SFC chapter on virtual assets should be read directly.

provisions.title: Money lender licensing and rate cap
provisions.summary: Section 3 excludes authorized institutions and persons lending to them. Section 7 prohibits unlicensed money lending, and s.24 makes lending above a 48% effective annual rate an offence, with unenforceable agreements.
provisions.counselNote: A bank does not need an MLO licence, but non-bank lending partners usually do unless exempt, for example as an AI subsidiary. Check their status and rate compliance before funding or co-branding. The text checked is as at 2022-12-30.

provisions.instrument: Re Gatecoin Ltd (in liquidation) [2023] HKCFI 914 (CFI, Linda Chan J, 31 March 2023, HCCW 18/2019)
provisions.title: Cryptocurrency as property held on trust
provisions.summary: The court held cryptocurrency is property capable of being held on trust. Under the 2018 terms there was no trust: they disclaimed fiduciary duty, the coins were pooled and the company treated them as its own in its accounts. For a residual group of customers who never accepted those terms, earlier terms with express trust language meant a trust existed.
provisions.counselNote: Outcome turned on contract wording and segregation, not on technology. A 2025 follow-up judgment dealt with distribution of the pooled assets.

checklist: **Classify every product** against the triage in the Activities tab before it enters the product pipeline, and record the analysis.
**Map every wallet and token flow** from customer app to ledger, custodian and counterparty, marking where private keys and client money sit.
**Confirm the route** for each activity: SFC registration under SFO s.119, Cap. 656 licence, HKMA discussion, or no licence needed with reasons.
**Open an HKMA conversation early** for custody, staking, stablecoin and tokenisation plans, and keep a record of what was discussed.
**Check each partner's status** on the SFC, HKMA or Companies Registry register, and re-check it at renewal and before promotions.
**Draft client-asset terms** that state trust or segregation status expressly, with no free right to use customer assets, and test them against a bank-insolvency scenario.
**Set the capital position** for any proprietary or collateral crypto exposure using the CRP-1 classification, and confirm limits and disclosure.
**Build the travel-rule and wallet-screening controls** into payments, with a rule for the HK$8,000 threshold and for missing counterparty data.
**Review all marketing and app copy** against AMLO s.53ZRE, Cap. 656 s.10, Cap. 155 ss.92 and 97, and the Code of Banking Practice.
**Fix the lending role** (lender, funder or account bank), and confirm MLO, SFO and outsourcing consequences in each platform contract.
**Set a watch list** for the pending bill, Basel review, circular updates and pilots, with named owners and review dates.
itAngle: **Key management:** Private-key generation, storage, signing and recovery are legal control points. Specify who can sign, how many approvals are needed and how training of signers is evidenced.
**Chain risk:** Forks, outages, oracle failures and smart contract bugs can change the customer's legal position. Ask engineering for a written risk assessment before any public-chain use.
**Data fields:** The travel rule needs originator and recipient data to travel with each transfer. Check that the payment messages, vendor tools and data stores can carry and retain it.
**Immutability and privacy:** Data on a ledger may not be erasable, which sits badly with PDPO retention duties. Keep personal data off-chain unless there is a documented basis.
**Vendor dependence:** Custody, analytics and tokenisation platforms are usually outsourced. Apply the vendor-contract playbook in Technology & outsourcing, and test exit and data-return clauses.
**Segregation in code:** Client assets must be separated in wallets and in ledgers. Ask for reconciliation reports that counsel can inspect, not only operational dashboards.
virtualBankNotes: **App-only distribution:** Every screen can be an advertisement. Review in-app placement of VA, stablecoin and partner offers under the advertising offences, and keep deposit and non-deposit products visually distinct.
**Fintech partners:** Most digital banks reach VA services through a licensed VATP or group partner. Contract for licence warranties, change notification, audit rights and clear client-asset terms.
**Group ecosystems:** A group may run its own exchange, wallet or token. Treat each group entity as a third party, avoid implied bank backing, and check conflicts and name-use rules.
**Limited capital headroom:** Group 2 crypto exposures are costly, and a young bank may lack the buffer. Test the business case against the exposure limit before design work.
**Deposit confusion:** Customers may assume wallet, token or yield balances are deposits protected by the DPS. Disclosure must say plainly what is and is not protected.

**Remote onboarding:** Wallet and VASP-linked customers are exposed to impersonation and mule risks. Align onboarding controls with the AML and fraud stage and current HKMA remote onboarding expectations.
pitfalls: **Calling a token a deposit or stablecoin loosely:** Labels in marketing can create offences or false protection expectations. Use the legal character of the product in all customer materials.
**Assuming a banking licence covers it:** It does not authorize stablecoin issuance, VA exchange operation or regulated SFO activity. Each needs its own route.
**Relying on a pilot as a right:** Project Ensemble, EnsembleTX and e-HKD are pilots. They give no entitlement and may change or end.
**Copying an old circular:** The joint circular, custody guidance and stablecoin circulars have been revised and superseded several times. Check the current version and date every time.
**Ignoring the partner's status:** An unlicensed or lapsed partner can make the bank's promotion an offence. Re-check registers, not just the contract warranty.
**Treating P2P as a bank-only matter:** Pooled structures can be securities or CIS, and fee flows can breach MLO s.27. Involve securities counsel early.

glossary.definition: A cryptographically secured digital representation of value used or intended as a medium of exchange, or carrying governance rights, and transferable electronically, as defined in AMLO s.53ZRA. Securities, SVF float and limited purpose tokens are excluded.
Virtual asset service provider: a business that provides VA services such as exchange, transfer or custody. In Hong Kong law the licensed class today is the VA trading platform operator.
Virtual asset trading platform: an SFC-licensed operator of a VA exchange under AMLO Part 5B. Banks typically deal through one by omnibus account.
A bank deposit liability recorded or represented as a token on a ledger. It remains a deposit under the Banking Ordinance and is not a stablecoin.
The requirement that originator and recipient information accompany a transfer, applied to VA transfers by AMLO Sch. 2 s.13A. A HK$8,000 threshold governs part of the data.
A wallet whose private key is controlled by the customer rather than by a financial institution or VASP. Also called a self-hosted wallet.
The secret cryptographic value that authorises transfer of a virtual asset. Whoever controls it controls the asset, so key management is central to custody.
A single account holding assets of many clients, such as a bank's account at a VATP for its customers. Client entitlements are tracked in the bank's own records.
Committing virtual assets to a validator in a proof-of-stake network to support it and earn rewards. It adds lock-up, slashing and withdrawal risks.
Code on a distributed ledger that executes automatically when conditions are met. Whether and when it is a legally binding contract is not settled in Hong Kong case law.
Decentralised finance: financial services run by smart contracts on public blockchains, often without an identifiable operator. Hong Kong has no dedicated DeFi regime.
A person whose business is making loans, licensed under the Money Lenders Ordinance unless exempt. Authorized institutions and their subsidiaries are excluded or exempt.
Online matching of lenders with borrowers for loans, usually unsecured. It may engage the MLO and, if pooled or structured as investments, the SFO.
The HKMA's initiative to support tokenisation, comprising a sandbox since August 2024 and a later EnsembleTX pilot for real-value tokenised deposit transactions. It is a pilot, not law.
The HKMA's research project on a central bank digital currency in Hong Kong dollars. The HKMA states that no policy decision has been made on a retail version.
A stablecoin that aims to keep value by reference to one or more official currencies, or other items the MA specifies. Only specified stablecoins are caught by ss.8 to 10 of Cap. 656.

intro: **Start with the triage:** Work through the questions in order for any new digital product, then open the matching activity card for the route, requirements and launch gates.
**Read the card in layers:** The route gives the headline answer, the requirements are the legal floor, and the gates are what counsel should confirm before launch.
**Check the regime label:** Each card shows whether the main regime is in force, transitional, proposed or a pilot. Proposals and pilots give no legal basis for launch.
**Use sources to verify:** Each card cites its main source first. Open it, check the date, and confirm the current position before relying on a summary.

triage.caption: Questions to ask, in order, to classify a new digital product.

items.label: Is it a claim to repayment of money?
items.note: Deposit or tokenised deposit under Cap. 155. Stop here and apply banking rules.

items.label: Is it stored value for payments?
items.note: SVF under Cap. 584; a bank relies on the s.8G deemed licence.

items.label: Is it a fiat-referenced stable-value token?
items.note: Specified stablecoin under Cap. 656; check issue, offer and advertising rules.

items.label: Is it a security or collective investment scheme?
items.note: SFO regime; the bank acts through registration under s.119.

items.label: Is it a virtual asset under s.53ZRA?
items.note: AMLO Part 5B and the joint circular; check the VATP and travel rule.

items.label: Does it involve making loans?
items.note: Bank lending under Cap. 155 and HKMA rules, or MLO for a non-bank lender.

items.label: None of the above?
items.note: Check limited purpose token status, advertising, bank-name rules and data protection. If the bank will hold the asset itself, see the crypto-assets balance sheet card.

activities.title: Distributing virtual-asset funds, ETFs and other VA-related products
activities.summary: The bank sells or arranges investment in products whose value tracks virtual assets, such as SFC-authorized spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs and VA-exposed funds. The bank does not hold the VA itself, but it takes on securities-type conduct duties.
activities.route: Yes, as an SFC [[registered institution]] (SFO s.119, normally Type 1 for dealing in securities), following the HKMA/SFC joint circular on VA-related activities and any terms attached to the registration. Tell your HKMA relationship team before launch.
require: **Registration:** An AI wanting to deal in securities-type products must be registered with the SFC under SFO s.119. The MA advises on fitness and propriety, and the SFC may impose conditions on the registration.

**Joint circular:** The HKMA and SFC joint circular of 22 December 2023 covers distribution of VA-related products. It replaced the October 2023 and January 2022 circulars and was supplemented on 30 September 2025.

**Complex products:** VA-related products that are complex products should meet the SFC complex-product sales requirements, including suitability. Whether a given spot VA ETF counts as complex was not confirmed in the sources found.

**Derivative products:** The joint circular allows retail offering of VA derivative products only if exchange-traded on a specified exchange and, for funds, authorised or approved for retail offering by the relevant regulator.

**Underlying fund rules:** SFC-authorized funds with VA exposure must follow the SFC circular on such funds (issued 22 December 2023, revised 7 April 2025 and updated 27 May 2026), including investing only in VAs tradable on SFC-licensed VATPs. The fund manager carries those duties, not the distributor.

**Tokenised wrappers:** A tokenised version of a non-SFO product is treated as the same product, with the same AI investor-protection standards (HKMA circular of 20 February 2024). This differs from a VA-related product.
gates: **Confirm the registration scope** covers the product type, and that any SFC conditions or HKMA terms on the bank's registration permit VA-related products. Get the answer in writing before the product committee meets.

**Classify each product** as complex or non-complex and as retail-eligible or professional-investor-only, with a documented rationale. Do this per product, not per product family, because treatment differs between ETFs, funds and derivatives.

**Build the suitability and knowledge test** for VA exposure, including a client risk-tolerance assessment and an exposure limit. Confirm the flow works in the app without nudging clients past warnings.
**Hold an HKMA conversation** on the proposed shelf, target segment and sales channel before launch. Keep the note of what was said and any feedback on risk disclosures.
**Review marketing and app copy** against the advertising offence in AMLO s.53ZRE and the SFC product-specific disclosures. Remove any promotion of unlicensed platforms or tokens.

**Agree the product-provider contract** to cover fund documents, risk disclosures, complaints, data sharing, termination and clawback of commissions. Align with the bank's vendor clause themes on outsourcing and audit.
**Obtain board or risk committee sign-off** on the VA risk appetite, the product governance process and the staff training plan for front-line sales.
watchFor: **Treating a fund as a pure securities sale:** Staff may sell it as an ordinary fund. Retail clients can have no VA experience, so the knowledge assessment and warnings matter as much as the product approval.
**Sliding into dealing:** If the bank starts handling VA orders itself, the activity moves to the Buying and selling virtual assets for customers card, which has extra conditions.

**Stale rules:** The joint circular was supplemented on 30 September 2025, and later circulars, including several of May 2026, also affect VA activities. Check the current text before relying on a law-firm summary or an older checklist.

activities.title: Buying and selling virtual assets for customers
activities.summary: The bank lets customers buy and sell VAs through the bank, typically by routing orders to an SFC-licensed VATP. Dealing is not yet a licensed VA service under AMLO, so the bank follows the joint circular while a statutory dealing regime is proposed.
activities.route: Yes, in practice, as an SFC [[registered institution]] with Type 1 registration, following the standard VA dealing terms and conditions under the joint circular of 22 December 2023, as supplemented, and dealing only through an omnibus account with an SFC-licensed VATP. The bank must not itself operate a VA exchange without an SFC licence.
require: **Current law:** AMLO Part 5B licenses only the operation of a VA exchange (Sch. 3B). Dealing, custody-only, advice and management are not Part 5B services today. Operating a VATP without an SFC licence is an offence under s.53ZRD.

**No AI exemption:** Part 5B has no general carve-out for AIs. Counsel's reading of s.53ZRD(2) is that only a licensed provider is exempt, so the bank should not operate the exchange itself. No regulator statement on this was found.

**Joint circular terms:** Intermediaries should deal only through an omnibus account with an SFC-licensed VATP and follow the standard terms and conditions for VA dealing. Separate conditions apply where the bank only introduces clients to a licensed VATP.

**Retail conditions:** The bank should assess the client's VA knowledge and risk tolerance, set an exposure limit and offer only VAs the licensed VATP makes available to retail investors. Circular paragraph numbers were not verified.

**Marketing reach:** Actively marketing a VA service to the public is treated as carrying on the business even from outside Hong Kong (s.53ZRB(3)-(5)). Advertising for an unlicensed platform is an offence (s.53ZRE).

**Recent relaxations:** HKMA guidance of 27 May 2026 addresses financing for VA dealing, shared order books and withdrawal safeguards, and a separate circular relaxes rules for licensed stablecoins. Read both before design.
gates: **Confirm registration and conditions.** Check that the bank's SFC registration and HKMA terms cover VA dealing. If not, plan the application and the HKMA/SFC engagement before any build work.
**Choose the VATP partner** from the SFC register of licensed VATPs, not from press lists. Record the licence check date and set up monitoring for any suspension or change of status.
**Settle the account structure** as an omnibus account at the VATP with ledger segregation inside the bank. Confirm who holds client VAs and how the bank reconciles them.

**Negotiate the partner contract** on custody and segregation, outage and incident notice, order execution, data and audit access, exit and migration, and liability. Treat it as a [[material outsourcing]] candidate.

**Decide on financing.** Treat any lending to buy VAs as out of scope until the HKMA guidance of 27 May 2026 is read in full and credit risk has approved. The SFC circular of 11 February 2026 limits VA financing to existing securities margin clients and limits VA collateral to Bitcoin and Ether. Sources conflict on the haircut.

**Run the AML design review** for VA transfers and travel rule duties, and the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline expectations on VASPs outside Hong Kong. See the Sending and receiving virtual-asset transfers card.
**Hold an HKMA conversation** and secure board and risk sign-off before the pilot, including a launch limit by client segment.
watchFor: **Drifting into operating an exchange:** If the bank matches orders or introduces buyers and sellers while client VAs come into its possession, it may be providing the Sch. 3B service and need an SFC licence.

**Assuming the proposals are law:** The SFC and the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau published consultation conclusions on 24 December 2025 on VA dealing and custodian licensing. As at the latest sources found (September 2026) no bill had been introduced, and commentators report that no transitional period is planned.

**Old circular versions:** The 28 January 2022 circular was superseded in October 2023, and that version on 22 December 2023. Retail access, stablecoin dealing and financing have all changed, so check the current text.

activities.title: Holding customers' virtual assets (custody)
activities.summary: The bank safekeeps VAs, tokenised securities or other tokenised assets for customers, which means controlling private keys. For a bank the main source of rules is the HKMA's custody guidance, because a statutory custodian licence is still only proposed.
activities.route: Yes, for an AI, provided it meets the HKMA's custody guidance (updated 27 May 2026) and has discussed the plan with the HKMA beforehand. Custody-only is not a Part 5B licensed service today; the proposed custodian licence is not law.
require: **HKMA guidance:** The HKMA's custody guidance for AIs, first issued 20 February 2024, was superseded and expanded by an update on 27 May 2026. Read the annex in full, as only some changes were confirmed.
**Scope:** The guidance covers VAs, tokenised securities and other tokenised assets held for clients. It does not cover assets the AI or its group holds for itself.

**Core standards:** The February 2024 guidance covered governance and risk management, segregation, safeguarding including private-key handling, outsourcing, disclosure, record keeping, reconciliation and AML/CFT. The 2026 update adds, among other things, training for transaction signers.

**Segregation:** Client assets should be kept apart from the bank's own and not lent, pledged or encumbered except in limited cases. Insolvency outcomes turn on terms and segregation. In Re Gatecoin, disclaimers and pooling defeated a trust for most customers; earlier express trust terms created one for others.

**Flows through the bank:** The joint circular expects client VA deposits and withdrawals to run through segregated accounts with partnered SFC-licensed VATPs or with AIs meeting HKMA custody standards. Paragraph reference unconfirmed.

**Staking:** An AI offering staking from custody should discuss it with the HKMA first (circular of 7 April 2025). The joint circular supplement of 30 September 2025 allows staking on conditions. See the card on Offering staking, DeFi access or crypto yield.
gates: **Engage the HKMA early** with the custody model, key architecture and sub-custodian choices. Confirm whether the 2026 update adds any notification or no-objection step, which the sources found do not settle.

**Settle the legal status of client assets** in the terms: express trust or equivalent segregation, no free right to use assets, and ledger separation. Re Gatecoin [2023] HKCFI 914 turned on terms, pooling and accounting treatment.

**Decide build or buy** for key management. If a sub-custodian or technology vendor is used, treat it as [[material outsourcing]] and cover audit, step-in, key recovery, insurance, incident notice and exit.

**Test the controls** for key generation, storage, signing authority, dual control, transaction-signer training and reconciliation. Obtain independent review, including a security assessment, before go-live.

**Map the insolvency position** under the bank's own resolution and winding-up regimes (Cap. 628 and Cap. 155 considerations), which Gatecoin did not address. Counsel's inference, so take a considered view.
**Align AML design** with travel rule duties in Sch. 2 s.13A and the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline on VASPs outside Hong Kong. See the Sending and receiving virtual-asset transfers card.
**Obtain board and risk sign-off** on custody risk appetite, loss-compensation arrangements and the incident and recovery playbook.
watchFor: **Taking it as licensed custody under statute:** No custody-only licence exists yet. The FSTB/SFC conclusions of 24 December 2025 propose one, reportedly without a transitional arrangement, so a bank should watch how AIs are treated in the bill.
**Contract wording that undermines segregation:** Terms that let the bank use client assets as its own, or pool them without clear records, can leave customers as unsecured creditors.
**Staking by accident:** A provider able to transfer client VAs while staking can fall into the proposed custodian regime, and the AI route for staking needs prior HKMA discussion.

activities.title: Issuing a fiat-referenced stablecoin
activities.summary: Issuing a [[fiat-referenced stablecoin]] in Hong Kong, or abroad where it references HKD, is a regulated stablecoin activity under Cap. 656. For a bank it is a separate licensed business from deposit-taking, and licences are scarce.
activities.route: Not under the banking licence alone. The bank needs a stablecoin licence from the MA under Cap. 656 (applying as a company or as an overseas AI, s.14). The first licences took effect on 10 April 2026, and the HKMA has signalled a high bar.
require: **Licence:** Carrying on, or holding out as carrying on, a regulated stablecoin activity without a licence or exemption is an offence under s.8. On indictment the maximum is a HK$5 million fine and 7 years' imprisonment. A banking licence does not count as a stablecoin licence.

**Perimeter:** Only a specified stablecoin is caught: one that purports to keep stable value wholly by reference to official currencies or other assets the MA specifies (s.4). Issuing outside Hong Kong is caught where the coin references HKD (s.5(1)). A tokenised deposit is a deposit, not a stablecoin (s.3(2)).

**Reserves and redemption:** Sch. 2 requires a segregated reserve pool worth at least par value of coins in circulation, in high-quality liquid assets, with independent audit and public disclosure (s.5). Holders must have a right to redeem at par as soon as practicable (s.6).

**Governance:** Licensees need fit and proper officers and controllers, relevant knowledge, risk management, data security and fraud controls, and a white paper for each coin type (Sch. 2 ss.7-9 and 13). An AI licensee must also have a stablecoin manager (s.66).

**Treatment of AIs:** The financial-resources test (including HK$25 million paid-up capital) and the dedicated-resources test in Sch. 2 ss.4 and 12 apply only to licensees that are not AIs. A bank's capital adequacy comes from the Banking Ordinance.

**AML/CFT:** A stablecoin licensee is a financial institution under AMLO and must meet Sch. 2 s.10 and the HKMA's AML/CFT guideline for licensed issuers. Expect CDD on issuers' customers, ascertaining ownership or control of every customer wallet, Travel Rule compliance and blockchain analytics.
gates: **Board business case:** Confirm the board has approved the use case, target holders and reasons a licence is realistic. The HKMA has said only a handful of licences would be granted at first and that the bar stays high.

**Classification memo:** Confirm a written analysis shows the product is a specified stablecoin and not a deposit, SVF float or security. If it is a deposit, follow the card on Issuing tokenised deposits instead.

**HKMA pre-application dialogue:** Confirm the current application form, timetable and expectations through early HKMA contact. Sch. 3 sets a licence fee of HK$113,020, but check the fee and form before filing.

**Structure decision:** Confirm whether issuance sits in the bank or in a ring-fenced affiliate. Check the Banking Ordinance interaction (receiving money for stablecoins is outside banking business under the s.2 proviso) and who is the stablecoin manager.

**Reserve and redemption design:** Confirm the reserve policy, trust or custody arrangement, auditor, and redemption terms. The supervision guideline, as summarised by law firms, expects redemption at par, usually within one business day. Read the text to confirm.

**Third-party contracts:** Confirm contracts with blockchain, wallet, custody and analytics vendors give audit and exit rights and the controls Sch. 2 s.5 expects over third parties. Treat them as material outsourcing where they qualify.
**Scam and brand controls:** Confirm monitoring and takedown for look-alike tokens and a customer warning page, and that no marketing runs before the licence is granted.
watchFor: **Pre-licence marketing:** Holding out as carrying on the activity is itself an offence under s.8. Soft launches, waitlists and public roadmaps need counsel review before they go live.
**Look-alike tokens:** On 28 April 2026 the HKMA warned of tokens using the tickers HKDAP and HSBC that the licensees had not issued. Expect the same for your brand.
**Offshore issuance:** A coin issued abroad that references HKD, even partly, is still caught by s.5(1). Group treasury or foreign branch plans must be checked against it.
**Guideline detail:** The HKMA supervision guideline text was not read for this card. A Hong Kong bank requirement for reserves is reported from LCQ11 of 24 June 2026 and is unconfirmed.

activities.title: Offering, distributing or accepting stablecoins
activities.summary: A bank may want to let customers buy, hold or spend stablecoins in its app, or accept them as payment. Cap. 656 regulates offering to the public, advertising and fraud, and it treats AIs as permitted offerors.
activities.route: Yes for licensed issuers' coins. An AI is a permitted offeror (s.9(5)), but the issue must be authorized by a stablecoin licence. Coins from unlicensed issuers can in practice go only to professional investors. Acceptance as payment has no express rule, so raise it with the HKMA.
require: **Offer offence:** It is an offence to offer, or hold oneself out as offering, a specified stablecoin unless an exception applies (s.9). Penalties match s.8: HK$5 million and 7 years on indictment.

**Permitted offeror:** The main exception needs both a permitted offeror and an issue authorized by a licence, whoever holds it. Permitted offerors include licensed issuers, AMLO-licensed VA service providers, SVF licensees, SFC Type 1 licensees and AIs (s.9(5)).

**Retail limit:** For coins not issued under an HKMA licence, the only class specified under s.9(3) is professional investors (L.N. 126 of 2025). Retail customers can therefore be offered only licensed issuers' coins. This is an inference from s.9(2) and the notice.

**Advertising:** Publishing an advertisement that holds out an unlicensed activity, or an offer outside s.9(2), is an offence where the publisher knows the facts (s.10). Defences cover reasonable steps and neutral conduits (s.10(4)-(6)).

**Fraud and misrepresentation:** Ss.11-12 apply to anyone, licensed or not, and cover offers and invitations. Maximum penalties on indictment are HK$10 million and 10 years (s.11) and HK$1 million and 7 years (s.12).

**Registered institutions:** A 27 May 2026 HKMA circular relaxes some VA-related requirements for registered institutions dealing in, advising on or managing coins of licensed issuers. Confirm which requirements change. It does not extend to other stablecoins.
gates: **Coin eligibility list:** Confirm the bank offers only coins whose issue is authorized by an HKMA licence. Re-check the HKMA register before each listing, and set a delisting trigger if the licence is revoked.

**Route to market:** Decide whether the bank offers as permitted offeror, refers customers to a licensed VATP, or uses a partner. Under the first, confirm the SFO registration position and any Type 1 or VA dealing activity (see the card on Buying and selling virtual assets for customers).

**HKMA conversation:** Confirm the HKMA is content with the product, wallet model and suitability approach. Also ask how it treats accepting licensed stablecoins as payment, which the research could not locate.
**Marketing sign-off:** Confirm compliance and legal review of every in-app placement, partner promotion and social post against s.10, with a record of the reasonable steps taken.

**Custody and wallet model:** Confirm who holds the coins and how customers withdraw to unhosted wallets. Cross-refer to the cards on Holding customers' virtual assets (custody) and Sending and receiving virtual-asset transfers.

**Partner contracts:** Confirm issuer and VATP agreements cover redemption access, disclosure of reserve reports, outage and depeg procedures, data sharing, and rights to suspend the coin at short notice.
**Customer disclosure:** Confirm risk disclosures say the coin is not a deposit and not protected by the Deposit Protection Scheme, and that redemption rights run against the issuer.
watchFor: **Unlicensed coins:** Offering a non-licensed coin to retail clients falls outside s.9(2). The exemption for professional investors does not help a mass-market app.
**Fake tickers:** The HKMA warned on 28 April 2026 of tokens using licensed issuers' names. Check contract addresses, not just names or tickers.
**Scope creep by notice:** The MA can add regulated activities by Gazette notice under s.5(4). None was found, but distribution or custody could be brought in without a new Ordinance.
**Relaxation limits:** The May 2026 circular was summarised from secondary sources. Do not assume it applies to an AI that is not a registered institution.

activities.title: Banking for stablecoin issuers: reserve accounts and custody of reserves
activities.summary: Licensed issuers must back their coins with a segregated reserve pool, and the Ordinance lets that pool be held through another person. That makes banks natural reserve account banks and custodians, with trust, segregation and AML duties.
activities.route: Yes, for a licensed issuer. Cap. 656 Sch. 2 s.5(1) lets the issuer maintain the pool through an arrangement with another person, and the HKMA supervision guideline expects reserves to sit with licensed banks or other custodians it accepts. Confirm with the HKMA whether bank custody of reserves is also caught by its custody guidance.
require: **Segregated pool:** Reserves must be a separate pool for each coin type, worth at least the par value of coins in circulation at all times, and kept apart from other funds (Sch. 2 s.5). The issuer remains responsible when a third party holds them.

**Protection from creditors:** The issuer must keep each pool adequately protected against its other creditors' claims in all circumstances (Sch. 2 s.5(4)). The duty is the issuer's, so expect it to seek trust, segregation and no-set-off terms from the bank.

**Asset quality:** Reserves must be high quality, highly liquid and low risk. The HKMA supervision guideline, as summarised by law firms, expects cash, deposits of up to three months and high-quality marketable debt securities.
**Trust structure:** The same summaries say the pool is held on trust and segregated, with licensed banks or other custodians acceptable to the HKMA, and with an independent legal opinion.

**Disclosure and audit:** Issuers must have independent attestation and audit, and publish their reserve policy, composition and audit results (Sch. 2 s.5). The bank will be asked for confirmations, balances and access to support these.

**AML/CFT:** The issuer is an AMLO financial institution, and the bank must still apply its own AML/CFT Guideline controls to the issuer as customer. See the card on Banking VASPs, trading platforms and stablecoin issuers.
gates: **Account mandate and trust terms:** Confirm the account or custody agreement states that assets are held for the reserve pool and not for the bank. It should bar set-off, charges and netting against the issuer's other debts to the bank.

**Licence verification:** Confirm the customer holds a stablecoin licence for the coin concerned before opening the account. For a pre-licence applicant, follow the card on Banking VASPs, trading platforms and stablecoin issuers and give no reserve role.

**Custody perimeter:** Confirm with the HKMA whether holding reserves counts as custodial services under its current digital-asset custody guidance. If it does, apply its governance and access-control expectations.

**Counterparty and concentration limits:** Confirm credit approval for reserve deposits, since a bank holding reserves may also be the issuer's counterparty risk. Check large exposure, liquidity and run-risk impact if redemptions are heavy.
**Information flows:** Confirm what the bank will provide to the issuer's auditor and the HKMA, within secrecy and PDPO limits, and agree a protocol for urgent confirmations.
**Insolvency playbook:** Confirm how the bank would act if the issuer failed, including holders' pro rata rights over the pool under Sch. 2 s.6, and how it responds to MA directions.
**Own-issuance conflicts:** If the bank is also a licensee, confirm separation between its own reserve pool and any services for other issuers, with approvals recorded.
watchFor: **Commingling:** Mixing reserve balances with the issuer's operating or the bank's own funds undermines the creditor protection the Ordinance requires. Use clearly named, separate accounts.
**Unconfirmed location rule:** LCQ11 of 24 June 2026 is reported to require reserves to be placed with Hong Kong banks. That reply has not been read, so treat the point as unverified.
**Overseas reserves:** A reserve held outside Hong Kong, for example by a group bank abroad, may not meet HKMA expectations. Check before offering cross-border arrangements.
**Dual role:** A bank that is both issuer and reserve bank for its own coin must show the pool is legally separate from the bank's own balance sheet.

activities.title: Issuing tokenised deposits
activities.summary: A tokenised deposit is a bank's ordinary deposit liability recorded or represented as a token on a ledger. It matters because it lets the bank offer programmable, ledger-based money without a stablecoin licence, and it is the settlement asset in the HKMA's Project Ensemble tests.
activities.route: Yes, under the bank's existing licence, because a token that is a [[deposit]] stays within the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155). No separate licence applies, but the bank should discuss the design with the HKMA early. If the token is not a deposit, Cap. 656 may apply.
require: **Legal character:** Cap. 656 s.3(2)(e) excludes from the stablecoin definition a digital representation of value that is a deposit under Cap. 155 s.2(1). So the legal test is whether the token is a claim to repayment of money received as a deposit, not the technology used.

**Deposit definition:** Cap. 155 s.2(1) defines a deposit as a loan of money, with listed exclusions including SVF floats and SVF deposits and specified stablecoins. Nothing in the definition removes a deposit because it is tokenised.

**No stablecoin route by default:** A banking licence does not authorize stablecoin issuance. A token that meets Cap. 656 s.3(1) and is not a deposit may be a stablecoin, and issuing it can be a regulated stablecoin activity needing a licence under Cap. 656 s.8. See the card on Issuing a fiat-referenced stablecoin.

**Deposit protection:** Cap. 581 s.2(1) takes the Cap. 155 meaning of deposit, and Sch. 1 s.1 lists exclusions such as bearer instruments (para (c)) and structured deposits (para (aa)). Sch. 1 has no tokenisation exclusion. The HKMA has not, on the research found, issued a statement on tokenised deposits and the DPS.

**Existing prudential rules:** The bank's existing capital, liquidity, operational resilience and outsourcing expectations still apply to a tokenised deposit platform. The Banking (Capital) Rules now include cryptoasset exposure provisions, such as Group 1a for tokenised traditional assets; check how they apply. No tokenised-deposit-specific HKMA circular was found.
gates: **Classify every token design** in writing against Cap. 155 s.2(1) and Cap. 656 s.3(1)-(2), and record why each design is a deposit, not a stablecoin, SVF float or security.

**Test bearer-style features** against Cap. 581 Sch. 1 s.1(c). Confirm the terms, ledger and transfer mechanics do not turn a protected deposit into an excluded instrument, and settle what customers are told about [[DPS]] cover.

**Open an HKMA conversation** before launch, covering ledger choice, governance, key management, finality of settlement and exit arrangements. Treat the absence of specific guidance as a reason to engage, not a licence to proceed.

**Paper the vendor stack.** If a platform provider or public network is involved, test it as a [[material outsourcing]] and agree audit, access, incident, step-in and [[exit plan]] clauses before signing.

**Settle customer terms** on redemption at par, transfer limits, wallet access, dormant and lost-key treatment, and how the on-ledger record relates to the bank's books. The books should be the legal record.

**Decide the test route.** Consider whether the bank joins an Ensemble pilot first (see the card on Joining e-HKD, Project Ensemble and other HKMA pilots) and obtain board and risk sign-off on the risk appetite.
watchFor: **Label drift:** Marketing a token as a stablecoin, or letting it be used as one, may pull it toward Cap. 656 even though the bank calls it a deposit.

**Reserve-pool design:** Ring-fencing assets behind the tokens looks like stablecoin reserves. Cap. 581 Sch. 1 s.1(j) excludes deposits of stablecoin reserve assets from DPS protection, a different treatment from ordinary deposits.

**Selling to the public:** Distribution of a tokenised deposit placed by customers should follow the conduct standards in the HKMA's 20 February 2024 tokenised products circular. This point is from secondary commentary; check the circular text.
**Pilot is not approval:** Taking part in Project Ensemble does not clear a commercial product. Confirm with the HKMA what is allowed outside the pilot.

activities.title: Issuing, distributing or holding tokenised bonds and funds
activities.summary: Tokenised bonds and funds are securities or fund interests whose ownership is recorded or represented on distributed ledger technology. A bank may act as distributor, dealer, custodian, settlement bank or issuer, and each role carries different obligations.
activities.route: Yes, within the bank's existing permissions, provided that securities activities run through its [[registered institution]] status with the SFC and HKMA supervision. Holding tokenised assets for clients means the bank should meet the HKMA's custody standards and notify the HKMA. Non-SFO tokenised products follow the HKMA's separate circular.
require: **Securities regime:** Dealing in, advising on or managing portfolios investing in tokenised securities is regulated like the underlying securities. SFC circular 23EC52 of 2 November 2023 applies to registered institutions, including AIs registered for Type 1, 4 and 9 activities.

**Due diligence:** Under 23EC52, an intermediary should do due diligence on the issuer, third-party vendors and the tokenisation arrangement, and be satisfied that risks are controlled. Named risks include ownership and recording of interests, forking, outages and cybersecurity.

**Issuer role:** An intermediary that is also the issuer remains responsible for the whole arrangement even if it outsources parts. Bearer-form tokenised securities on public permissionless networks raise extra custody points such as immobilisation, segregation and private-key management.

**Custody standards:** The HKMA's custody guidance for digital assets (first issued 20 February 2024, updated 27 May 2026) covers risk assessment, governance, conflicts, segregation from the AI's own assets, key management and recovery, disclosure of risks and AML/CFT. It reaches tokenised bonds and funds held for clients.

**Non-SFO products:** For tokenised products that are not regulated under the SFO, the HKMA's circular of 20 February 2024 expects the usual conduct rules plus controls for tokenisation risks: product due diligence, disclosure, staff expertise and custody.

**Authorized funds:** On 20 April 2026 the SFC replaced its 2 November 2023 circular on tokenising SFC-authorized products and issued a circular on secondary trading of tokenised authorised products on SFC-licensed VATPs, mainly for tokenised open-ended funds.
gates: **Sort each product into a regime.** SFO security, SFC-authorized fund, non-SFO tokenised product, or non-security virtual asset covered by the joint circular of 22 December 2023. Record the reasoning and the circular that applies.

**Confirm registration scope** for the bank's SFC activity types and check the registered-institution conditions. Do not assume tokenised securities fall within existing Type 1, 4 or 9 permissions without checking the circular text.

**Notify the HKMA** before holding tokenised assets for clients if not already doing so. The February 2024 custody circular gave existing providers six months from the circular date to confirm compliance with its Annex. New entrants must first discuss plans with the HKMA.

**Diligence the platform and network.** Document tests of the issuer, platform provider, ledger and smart contracts, including record-keeping, finality, outage and fork scenarios. Treat any platform as a [[material outsourcing]] where it qualifies.

**Fix settlement and custody mechanics.** Who holds keys, how client assets are segregated, and how settlement cash moves, including whether a tokenised deposit or stablecoin settles trades. See the card on Issuing tokenised deposits.
**Obtain board and risk sign-off** on the product shelf, suitability and disclosure approach, and staff competence for a technology-led product.
watchFor: **Superseded guidance:** The SFC replaced its 2 November 2023 circular on tokenising SFC-authorized products on 20 April 2026. Intermediary circular 23EC52 still applies, so check both texts.

**Trading venue gap:** Secondary trading of tokenised authorised funds happens on SFC-licensed VA trading platforms. A bank acting only as distributor or custodian should not offer matching itself without the right licence. See the card on Buying and selling virtual assets for customers.
**Public network risk:** Holding bearer-form tokens on a public permissionless network is a custody-heavy case. Assume the HKMA will probe key control and segregation.

activities.title: Joining e-HKD, Project Ensemble and other HKMA pilots
activities.summary: The HKMA runs pilots on tokenised money and assets, including e-HKD, Project Ensemble and its real-value phase EnsembleTX, and the cross-border Project mBridge. They are tests, not law, but they shape what the HKMA expects of banks that later launch tokenised products.
activities.route: Yes, by invitation or application to the HKMA, on terms the HKMA sets for each pilot; pilot status does not itself take an activity outside Cap. 155, the SFO or other regimes. Joining a pilot does not authorize a commercial launch, so the bank should confirm the legal basis for any live value.
require: **Pilot status:** These initiatives are HKMA programmes, not legislation. Terms come from the pilot rules, participation agreements and any sandbox conditions, so counsel should read those documents, not look for a statute.

**Ensemble history:** The HKMA unveiled Project Ensemble in March 2024 and launched its sandbox on 28 August 2024 for interbank settlement tests using experimental tokenised money. On 13 November 2025 it announced EnsembleTX for real-value transactions through 2026.

**EnsembleTX scope:** First use cases are tokenised deposits in tokenised money market fund transactions and in liquidity and treasury management. Interbank settlement initially uses the HKD RTGS system, with planned upgrades to tokenised central bank money; the upgrade is not confirmed as live.
**e-HKD position:** The e-HKD pilot Phase 2 report of 28 October 2025 reported the pilot results and moved priority toward wholesale use. The HKMA's page states no policy decision on a retail e-HKD.

**mBridge:** Project mBridge reached minimum viable product in June 2024. The BIS announced on 31 October 2024 that it was handing the platform to participating central banks, calling it a graduation. The HKMA is a founding participant, but no primary HKMA statement on its current participation was found.

**Normal rules still apply:** Real-value pilot activity by an [[authorized institution]] remains subject to Cap. 155, AML/CFT duties and prudential expectations unless the HKMA says otherwise in writing.
gates: **Obtain the pilot documents** and confirm in writing the HKMA's stated legal position on live value, liability, data use and exit from the pilot. Do not rely on press releases for contract terms.

**Check participant lists** against the HKMA's EnsembleTX Annex A, which was not retrieved here. Secondary lists of participating banks conflict, so confirm any statement about peers, including whether digital banks take part.
**Map pilot activity to existing regimes.** Deposits, SFO activities, custody, AML/CFT and data protection. State which regime applies to each pilot flow before the first test transaction.
**Agree vendor and ledger terms** for the pilot platform, covering security, access, incident reporting, data location and termination. Keep the pilot out of production systems unless approved.
**Set success and stop criteria**, including a decision point for moving to a commercial product. Link to the card on Issuing tokenised deposits so that pilot learning feeds the product approval.
**Brief the board and risk committee** on pilot scope, losses the bank could bear, and reputational points, and record the approval.
watchFor: **Pilot is not approval:** Press coverage of firsts, such as reported live cross-bank tokenised deposit transfers, shows what was tested. It does not show that the HKMA has cleared a product for customers.
**Retail e-HKD assumptions:** No decision has been made on a retail e-HKD. Planning a customer product that depends on one would rest on a policy that does not exist.
**Moving plans:** Tokenised Exchange Fund Bills and a CMU OmniClear platform appear only in secondary reporting. Treat them as plans until a primary source confirms dates.
**Single-bank claims:** Participant announcements are not HKMA findings. No official EnsembleTX evaluation had been found as at October 2026.
